I still enjoy having control over my digital life, learning new things, and tinkering with technology.It’s just removed a lot of the friction that made me lose some of my enthusiasm for it over the years.And now, I’m having a lot of fun with it again.

Sources indicate that having some additional computing power available gives me more room to experiment. And there’s something quite satisfying about having a small box at home running a growing collection of services that I use in my everyday life.Building my own toolsBut it’s not just about self-hosting existing software. AI has also changed how I approach problems for which there isn’t an existing piece of software that does exactly what I want.Previously, I would often spend quite some time searching for a suitable open-source project, comparing different alternatives, and figuring out how to make one of them work for my particular use case.These days, for smaller problems, building my own solution has become a much more attractive option.I’ve recently built tools to automatically download invoices, e-papers or Linux ISOs.I can build (or have AI build) these tools in Go, my preferred programming language, and tailor them to my exact needs.They don’t need to support every possible use case, have an elaborate user interface, or be particularly interesting to anyone other than me. I don’t need to turn every little tool into a proper open-source project with extensive documentation and support for other people’s use cases. They just need to solve my problem.What I particularly enjoy is how well this complements my increasingly automated infrastructure. Building a small tool has become easier, and so has building a container image for it, deploying it, and keeping it running.The entire process, from having an idea to having something actually running on my home server, requires much less effort than it used to.Just because I can doesn’t mean I shouldOf course, there are downsides to all of this.Every additional service is another thing that needs to be maintained. AI-generated software isn’t exempt from bugs, security problems, or technical debt. And having an AI agent make changes to my infrastructure doesn’t absolve me of the responsibility of understanding those changes.There’s also the temptation to build or deploy things simply because I can. When implementing an idea becomes so easy, it’s perhaps more key than ever to occasionally ask myself whether it’s actually worth implementing in the first place.On the other hand, self-hosting is a hobby for me. Not everything I do needs to be economically sensible or particularly useful. Sometimes, experimenting with something new is the whole point.And with much of the routine maintenance automated, adding another service doesn’t necessarily mean adding as much recurring work as it used to.A somewhat ironic development?I find it somewhat ironic that AI, a technology largely dominated by massive tech companies, is helping me become a little less dependent on those very companies in other areas of my digital life.I’m aware that this also creates a new kind of dependency. But the software and infrastructure configurations I create with the help of AI can continue to exist independently of the AI services I used to create them. And since I mostly use open-weight models, I have a wide range of providers to choose from.What I appreciate most, however, isn’t necessarily the time I’m saving. It’s that I’m more inclined to actually pursue the little ideas I have.I’m trying out technologies I’ve been curious about for years. I’m automating things that I’ve wanted to automate for a long time. I’m building little tools for myself. I’m tinkering with hardware again.AI hasn’t fundamentally changed why I like self-hosting. I still enjoy having control over my digital life, learning new things, and tinkering with technology.It’s just removed a lot of the friction that made me lose some of my enthusiasm for it over the years.And now, I’m having a lot of fun with it again.

While Saatva, Tempur-Pedic, and DreamCloud are offering the best Black Friday mattress deals we've seen this year, all three brands are also behind some of 2026's best mattress toppers. But which premium mattress topper should side sleepers buy in the Black Friday sales?

Industry observers note that we've tested the Saatva Graphite, Tempur-Adapt + Cooling and the DreamCloud mattress toppers and they each deliver the signature luxury of their respective brands' mattresses. This comparison guide will help you choose which topper is right for you if you're a side sleeper in need of extra comfort.

For the latest price cuts, also see our guide to the best Black Friday mattress deals live.

Recent findings suggest that A comfy topper from a leading sleep brand, but its retention of excess heat lets it down. Though if feel cold in bed, this could be ideal.

According to recent reports, the 3"-thick Graphite Memory Foam Mattress Topper is the most popular entry in Saatva's bed topper collection. Its body-cradling foam supports all sleep positions, including side sleeping, while its anchor straps keep the topper in place. However, despite the infusion of graphite, this memory foam topper can trap body heat.

Sink-in softness, contouring that hugs your curves to relieve pressure, and all-night cooling to keep you at the right temperature for sleep.

In a recent development, the Tempur-Adapt + Cooling is the most top-rated mattress topper we've ever tested, as it uses Tempur-Pedic's propriety Tempur-Material to provide softening comfort for side sleepers and hard beds. The addition of a cooling cover prevents heat build-up, but be aware that there's no official sleep trial.

A good cooling memory foam topper to soften the area under your shoulders, hips and knees, but the lack of anchor straps is frustrating.

It has been revealed that the DreamCloud Softer Mattress Topper is made from a 2" slab of gel memory foam that our testers found to be cushioning along the shoulders and hips, making it ideal for side sleepers. Its breathable cover complete with "cooling yarns" means the DreamCloud Topper doesn't overheat. However, there's no anchor straps to prevent shifting.

It has been revealed that all three mattress toppers are 3" thick and use memory foam to cushion firm beds. While each works well for side sleepers, their distinct features make them better suited for different types of side sleepers.

According to recent reports, for instance, the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam Mattress Topper caters to all sleep styles, making it ideal for side sleepers who sometimes switch to back or front sleeping — or side sleepers who share a bed with someone who sleeps in a different position. In contrast, the DreamCloud and Tempur-Adapt have a plush feel best suited to side sleepers only.

The Tempur-Adapt + Cooling Mattress Topper has a cooling cover to prevent side sleepers from overheating (the Saatva Graphite, on the other hand, is prone to heat build-up). The DreamCloud Softer Mattress Topper also sleeps cooler than the Saatva Graphite, but doesn't have the washable cover with anchor straps. Still, it's the cheapest of the three, starting at $179 (the Saatva starts at $225; the Tempur-Adapt at $259).

Recent findings suggest that we test mattress toppers in key areas, particularly in temperature regulation and comfort and support. We then give each area a score out of 5.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Industry observers note that when testing comfort and support, our testers sleep on each topper in the three main sleep styles (back, side, and stomach) to see how comfortable and supportive it is in each position. The Saatva Graphite performed the best in this area, scoring a near-perfect 4.5/5, because its medium-firm feel supports all sleep styles.

It has been revealed that in comparison, the Tempur-Adapt's 3.5/5 score may seem low, but that's because it's too soft to support back and front sleepers. For side sleepers only, the Tempur-Adapt + Cooling provides incredible pressure relief. The DreamCloud also lost a point for its softness, but it's still a great topper for side sleepers.

As for temperature regulation (how well a topper maintains a comfortable temperature), the Tempur-Adapt's cooling cover upgrade scored the highest points. Meanwhile, the DreamCloud's breathable cover, while not cool-to-the-touch, prevented overheating. The Saatva Graphite scored the lowest, as our lead tester found it was prone to trapping heat.

Here's a close-up look at each mattress topper, exploring their respective designs and prices, plus who we do and don't recommend them to...

The Saatva Graphite Memory Foam Mattress Topper is a 3" slab of graphite-infused memory foam that's enveloped in a breathable, antimicrobial organic cotton cover (the same material used for the covers of the best Saatva mattresses).

Sources indicate that despite a naturally cool cover and a graphite-infusion, our testers found the Saatva Graphite's memory foam to trap heat. However, both Saatva customers and our testers agree that the memory foam's medium-firm feel adds plenty of comfort and support to mattresses.

It has been revealed that the Saatva Graphite (or any other Saatva toppers, for that matter) are pretty much never included in the Saatva Black Friday sales, let alone the monthly Saatva sales. That means you'll always pick up a Saatva Graphite from $225 in a twin. Extras include a generous 180-night sleep trial and a so-so one-year warranty.

In a recent development, the 3" Temur-Adapt + Cooling Mattress Topper is actually an upgrade of the original Tempur-Adapt Mattress Topper. We found the original's use of pressure-relieving Tempur-Material was great for side sleeping, but was also prone to heat build-up.

That's why were so pleased when the + Cooling upgrade added a cooling cover, with out lead tester impressed with the difference it made. While not a great mattress topper for those who sleep on their back or front, it's a top pick for side sleepers who need to soften hard beds.

The Tempur-Adapt + Cooling Topper is the only one out of the three toppers to be included in the Black Friday mattress topper sales. This means you'll save up to 30% on all sizes in this month's Tempur-Pedic sales, with a twin now down to $259 (was $339). Disappointingly, there's no sleep trial, but you will get a generous 10-year warranty.

DreamCloud is known for its flagship DreamCloud Classic Hybrid, a luxury hybrid mattress at a medium-range price, so it's only fitting that it would offer a bed topper at a fraction of the cost of its mattresses, too.

The DreamCloud Softer Topper is one of two DreamCloud toppers; the other is called the DreamCloud Firmer Topper, which is designed to give a (you guessed it) a firmer feel. The DreamCloud Softer Topper is made from 2" of gel-infused memory foam, which our testers say provides a contouring feel for side sleepers.

The DreamCloud Softer Topper may not be on sale for Black Friday (no surprises there, it's never in the DreamCloud sales) but that doesn't stop it from being the cheapest option. A twin is priced at $179, and comes with a 100-night sleep trial, a one-year warranty, and free shipping and returns.

Industry observers note that for side sleepers who are looking to soften a hard bed, we'd reccomend looking at the Temour-Adapt + Cooling or the DreamCloud Softer Topper. Both have a plusher feel than the Graphite and are great at regulating temperature, though those who need a bigger comfort boost should go for the thicker Tempur-Adapt.

Those looking for the most cost-effective, on the other hand, should pick the under-$200-for-a-queen DreamCloud. Meanwhile, the Saatva Graphite is best for side sleepers who prefer a firmer feel, combination sleepers, and couples with different sleep styles.

Industry News: This Oversold Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock Will Skyrocket 123% in 2027, According to Wall Street

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cloud infrastructure stocks have been hammered lately as investors have been rotating out of this sector for multiple reasons.
  • According to recent reports, inflationary conditions led the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates in September, and it could make a similar move in December.
  • According to recent reports, this explains why investors have been booking profits in AI infrastructure stocks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Harsh Chauhan – Nov 26, 2026 at 1:27PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than DigitalOcean ›.

Cloud infrastructure stocks have been hammered lately as investors have been rotating out of this sector for multiple reasons.

According to recent reports, inflationary conditions led the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates in September, and it could make a similar move in December. A high-interest rate scenario doesn't bode well for companies investing heavily in artificial intelligence (AI) data center infrastructure, as they will have to contend with higher borrowing costs.

According to recent reports, this explains why investors have been booking profits in AI infrastructure stocks. DigitalOcean (DOCN -3.09%) has also borne the brunt of the broader sell-off in cloud stocks, with shares of the organization losing 55% of their value over the past six months. However, a closer look at DigitalOcean's growth and prospects indicates that the sell-off may be overdone.

DigitalOcean offers on-demand cloud infrastructure services to small and medium-sized companies, developers, and start-ups. DigitalOcean's customers can rent computing resources to run AI workloads in the cloud without investing in expensive infrastructure of their own. The company also offers platform-as-a-service (PaaS) solutions, enabling users to build, customize, and deploy AI applications.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

So, DigitalOcean provides a full-stack cloud infrastructure platform that integrates hardware and software. Customers can build AI agents, run business analytics, detect fraud, create chatbots, summarize documents, and perform other tasks using its AI-native cloud platform. The good part is that DigitalOcean's AI services are in solid demand.

The company released its third-quarter results earlier this month, and it became clear that AI is a key catalyst. Its Q3 revenue increased by 40% year over year to $321 million. The company's annual run rate revenue (ARR) also increased by a similar magnitude to $1.28 billion. However, what's worth noting is that DigitalOcean's ARR from AI customers increased by 288% year over year to $376 million.

The robust adoption of DigitalOcean's AI services explains why it expects its revenue growth rate to ramp up next year. DigitalOcean expects its revenue growth to accelerate to 45% year over year in the current quarter. Even better, it sees a 60% jump in revenue next year, which is well above its prior guidance of 50% growth.

Recent findings suggest that another crucial point worth noting is that DigitalOcean's software stack is boosting its ARR. I already pointed out that DigitalOcean doesn't make money by just renting out hardware. The firm points out that customers are using its software solutions to build and deploy agentic AI applications, which is driving up DigitalOcean's revenue per megawatt (MW) of cloud computing capacity it deploys.

DigitalOcean is on track to end 2026 with 75 MW of active data center capacity. That number is poised to double next year, and it aims to further increase its capacity in 2028. This explains why analysts expect DigitalOcean to clock solid revenue growth in 2028 as well.

DOCN Revenue Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts.

Importantly, the increasing adoption of its software offerings is poised to drive significant acceleration in earnings per share (EPS) growth.

DOCN EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts.

The impressive revenue and earnings growth that DigitalOcean is poised to deliver is likely to send its shares soaring, according to Wall Street.

Recent findings suggest that digitalOcean's median 12-month price target of $160 implies potential upside of 123%, according to estimates compiled by CNN. It is worth noting that 16 of the 18 analysts covering DigitalOcean rate the stock as a buy.

Sources indicate that it is easy to see why analysts are bullish about its stock price trajectory over the coming year. DigitalOcean's growth rate is picking up, and it trades at an attractive 8 times sales right now. The U.S. technology sector has an average sales multiple of 5.6, and the slight premium that DigitalOcean enjoys is attributable to its improving growth profile.

I won't be surprised to see DigitalOcean trading at a slightly higher sales multiple after a year, driven by a stronger top-line jump. Assuming it trades at 10 times sales, and its top line reaches $1.96 billion in 2027, the organization's market cap could increase to $19.6 billion. That's 130% higher than the current market cap, suggesting that DigitalOcean indeed has the potential to live up to Wall Street's expectations and skyrocket next year.

#143765. Breaking: Judge orders Apple to produce 3,200 documents in Epic Games dispute

Breaking: Judge orders Apple to produce 3,200 documents in Epic Games dispute

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (918 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that A federal judge has ordered Apple to produce a random sample of 3,200 documents for Epic Games to review, following Epic’s allegations that Apple improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions.
  • With Apple and Epic trading arguments in the Supreme Court over whether the civil contempt ruling against Apple should stand, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.
  • In August, Apple submitted its proposal to the district court, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A federal judge has ordered Apple to produce a random sample of 3,200 documents for Epic Games to review, following Epic’s allegations that Apple improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions. Here are the details.

With Apple and Epic trading arguments in the Supreme Court over whether the civil contempt ruling against Apple should stand, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.

In August, Apple submitted its proposal to the district court, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%. Epic, however, is disputing not just the basis for those proposed rates, but also Apple’s handling of document production in the proceedings.

Earlier this month, Epic accused Apple of improperly withholding more than 122,000 documents matching a set of search terms agreed upon by both companies to help identify documents that could shed light on how Apple arrived at those rates.

[…] Apple is withholding well over 99% of the documents returned by running the agreed-to search terms on the files of the four custodians Apple states decided on the proposed fee (Tim Cook, Eddy Cue, Carson Oliver, and Kevan Parekh (Apple’s latest CFO)) and three other key individuals (Nate Barton, Alex Roman, and Phil Schiller). Apple claims these withheld documents are not relevant to this proceeding-even though they hit on case-specific terms such as “proffer,” “contempt,” “injunction,” and “link-out.” To put this into context, while Apple produced 632 custodial documents returned by these search terms (including families), Apple is withholding over 122,000 based on a claim of non-responsiveness.

Apple, in turn, pushed back against Epic’s accusations, saying the search terms were overly broad and had captured large numbers of documents unrelated to the proceedings.

It has been revealed that […] at least 95% of the Initial Custodian Document Population hit on generic terms […]. These sweeping terms do not just increase the total volume of the Initial Custodian Document Population, they also captured highly sensitive and irrelevant documents, such as Apple employees’ personal tax or financial records, medical records, documents discussing unannounced products, documents containing passwords, investor-relations materials, and privileged or protected legal communications.

The company also asked the court to reject Epic’s motion to order it to produce all non-privileged documents matching the agreed-upon search terms, and alternatively suggested submitting a randomized, statistically significant sample of the documents it deemed nonresponsive to a Special Master for independent review.

As it turns out, neither tech giant got exactly what it originally wanted, but the judge ruled largely in Epic’s favor on how to determine whether Apple had improperly withheld documents.

Following a hearing in which both companies presented their respective proposals for how a randomized sampling of the documents should be conducted, Magistrate Judge Thomas S. Hixson decided to adopt Epic’s proposal, which called for Apple to produce a random sample of 3,200 documents it had previously deemed nonresponsive, along with their associated document families, for Epic itself to review.

All documents in the sample will be drawn from the files of the seven Apple custodians referenced in Epic’s original motion.

Apple, by contrast, had suggested a considerably smaller sample of 383 documents, arguing that this would be statistically significant at a 95% confidence level.

In his decision, Judge Hixson agreed that Epic had legitimate reasons to question Apple’s reasons for withholding the documents:.

Sources indicate that apple’s responsiveness rate is so dramatically low that it raises red flags. With Apple screening out more than 99% of the documents that hit on the agreed search terms, it is unreasonable to ask Epic to believe that Apple is making these responsiveness calls in good faith. That is particularly true in this case, in which Judge Gonzalez Rogers has sanctioned Apple for its large-scale abuse of the attorney-client privilege for the purpose of obscuring the evidence.

Judge Hixson also rejected Apple’s suggestion that a Special Master conduct the review, arguing that given the level of familiarity with the case required to assess the relevance of these documents, Epic was the only practical option for determining whether Apple had systematically misclassified them.

Realistically, the only person who has the practical ability to determine if Apple has been systematically mis-coding documents as nonresponsive is its opponent, Epic.

In his decision, the judge agreed with Apple that the organization should be allowed to review the documents for privileged and sensitive information before producing them to Epic, and authorized Apple to designate all documents produced as part of the exercise as Attorneys’ Eyes Only.

Importantly, Judge Hixson has not yet determined whether Apple systematically misclassified responsive documents as nonresponsive, nor has he imposed the daily monetary sanctions originally requested by Epic.

Apple now has until December 8 to complete the document production, with Epic having until December 15 to file any objections, and Apple until December 22 to respond.

Better Defense Stock to Own in 2027: Lockheed Martin vs. L3Harris Technologies

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (741 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, lockheed Martin (LMT +2.15%) and L3Harris Technologies (LHX +1.48%) are top defense stocks.
  • Lockheed Martin's shares have soared this year, up more than 18% as I write this, while L3Harris' have slumped by more than 13%.
  • Here's a quick comparison of these two defense stocks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By James Halley – Nov 26, 2026 at 1:32PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Lockheed Martin ›.

According to recent reports, lockheed Martin (LMT +2.15%) and L3Harris Technologies (LHX +1.48%) are top defense stocks. Each stock has its advantages. Lockheed is a more stable stock with lower price volatility and a higher-yielding dividend. L3Harris, on the other hand, is showing more growth and benefits from higher margins.

Lockheed Martin's shares have soared this year, up more than 18% as I write this, while L3Harris' have slumped by more than 13%.

Here's a quick comparison of these two defense stocks.

Industry observers note that F-35 Stealth fighter jet. Image source: Lockheed Martin.

Sources indicate that lockheed Martin is a much larger company, with nearly three times L3Harris' market cap and employee count. The company's third-quarter backlog of $292 billion provides around 3.6 years of revenue visibility, substantially deeper than L3Harris' 2.25 years for its $53.2 billion backlog.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

It has been revealed that lockheed management is predicting high single-digit growth across all four of its business segments in 2027, led by F-35 sustainment/production and a $52.5 billion multiyear award for PAC-3 MSE interceptor missiles. That scale allows the tech giant to thrive even if one segment falters.

As a specialist in defense electronics, resilient communications, and propulsion, L3Harris generated a 15.9% segment operating margin in the third quarter, roughly 500 basis points higher than Lockheed Martin. L3Harris reported third-quarter earnings per share (EPS) of $3.28, up 33% year over year, prompting management to raise full-year EPS guidance to a range of $12.25 to $12.35, an increase of 44% at the midpoint.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

Industry observers note that lockheed, on the other hand, saw its third-quarter EPS slip by 11% to $6.44. It reaffirmed full-year EPS of between $29.35 and $30.25, a 38% gain at the midpoint.

Both companies have above-average dividend yields. At their current share prices, Lockheed's dividend yield is 2.42% while L3Harris' is 1.94%. Lockheed has increased its dividend for 24 consecutive years, while L3Harris has raised its dividend for 25 consecutive years. L3Harris has been more aggressive in increasing its dividend over the past decade, raising it by more than 135%, compared to just more than 89% for Lockheed, which could be an advantage in a stock-to-stock matchup.

Despite its share gain this year, Lockheed's stock is trading at a better price point. Its forward price-to-earnings ratio is slightly more than 18 times earnings estimates compared to more than 20 for L3Harris.

In a recent development, lockheed's biggest problem is that it is the lead on massive hardware programs, such as the F-35, F-16, C-13, and Sikorsky helicopters, and, as such, has lower operating margins, around 10.8% as of the third quarter. It is also affected more by fixed-price development or production charges. It stands to lose more, too, if a Democratic-controlled Congress tightens defense spending.

L3Harris carries more debt, with a debt-to-earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) ratio of 3.1, compared to 1.9 for Lockheed, and its debt payments could easily weigh on its earnings growth. L3Harris carries a heavier debt load relative to its size, with $9 billion in net long-term debt. Much of that is due to the manufacturer's $4.7 billion acquisition of Aerojet Rocketdyne in 2023.

However, L3Harris plans to sell a majority stake in its space propulsion and power Systems business to AE Industrial for $845 million, while retaining a 40% ownership stake in the newly created Rocketdyne venture, which includes manufacturing and selling RS-25 rocket engines.

It has been revealed that deciding which stock is best really comes down to your investing needs. Lockheed certainly offers more stability, though with less growth potential.

L3Harris is expected to see more revenue and earnings growth, though its higher valuation shows some of that expected growth is already priced into the stock. If I had to choose, Lockheed is the safer pick because of its scale, better dividend, and lower valuation.

  • According to recent reports, we've tested 170+ mattresses at Tom's Guide to find the best mattresses of 2026 for all sleepers, body types and budgets.
  • Best for all sleep styles and for back painThe Saatva Classic is highest scoring mattress we've tested, delivering excellent pressure relief and cooling comfort in every sleep position.
  • Best value for couples and for heavier peopleWhile the DreamCloud lacks the luxury trimmings of the Saatva, it delivers good back support, pressure relief and edge support at a third of the cost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, we've tested 170+ mattresses at Tom's Guide to find the best mattresses of 2026 for all sleepers, body types and budgets. After testing them across all four key areas of a mattress that most affect sleep comfort (see our mattress methodology for more), three mattresses stand head and shoulders above the rest when it comes to performance and sleep comfort for the price in this year's Black Friday mattress sales:.

Best for all sleep styles and for back painThe Saatva Classic is highest scoring mattress we've tested, delivering excellent pressure relief and cooling comfort in every sleep position. However, like the Helix, the Saatva isn't designed to support co-sleepers who weigh over 300lbs each – but the DreamCloud can. The Saatva is currently on sale for the best price we've seen since Labor Day, with a queen costing $1,804 (was $2,229).

Best value for couples and for heavier peopleWhile the DreamCloud lacks the luxury trimmings of the Saatva, it delivers good back support, pressure relief and edge support at a third of the cost. Yes it retained some heat during our cooling test, but not enough to scare off hot sleepers. Right now the DreamCloud is even better value than usual with a queen priced $699 and bundled with $599 of free bedding – it's rare to see free gifts with this.

Best for side sleepers with hip painThere isn't much separating the Helix and Saatva on paper, but from our testing we know that the feel of these luxury hotel-style mattress is different. While Saatva keeps you on top of the bed, Helix lets you sink in for a deep body-hug. That alone makes it the better choice if you have shoulder and hip pain when side sleeping. There's 25% off for Black Friday, with a queen priced $1,874 (was $2,498).

For the latest price cuts, see our Black Friday mattress deals tracked live guide.

According to recent reports, we put the Saatva Classic, the DreamCloud Classic Hybrid, and the Helix Midnight Luxe through the same set of standardised lab tests. We also analysed each mattress in terms of value for money. Here's how each mattress stacks up:.

Industry observers note that good pressure relief in a mattress combines two things: cushioning at the touch points, to reduce pressure build-up, and support for your spine to prevent strain or 'hammocking'. In other words, it's the 'aaah' feeling you get when you climb into a mattress that's just right for you. The Saatva, DreamCloud and Helix scored well in this area.

In a recent development, the Saatva earned a 5 out of 5 pressure relief test score for all sleep positions. (We tested the Luxury Firm Saatva Classic but it's available in three feels: Plush Soft, Luxury Firm and Firm). The surface contours lightly to your body, but springs back instantly to deliver constant and responsive pressure relief.

The Helix scored a 4.5 out of 5 score in the same test, with sink-in foams cushioning our shoulders and hips. While it's the best mattress for side sleepers, it didn't score full marks like the Saatva because it wasn't as responsive – the foams took longer to bounce back, and some of our testers found the Helix harder to move around on.

The DreamCloud Classic scored a 4 out of 5 in our pressure relief test, which is still an excellent score. It's lower than the Saatva and Helix because because contouring isn't quite as effective, and the materials took longer than the Helix to bounce back. There was also less lumbar support, but still impressive for a mid-range bed-in-a-box.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

If you're waking up most nights because you're too hot or too cold, you need a matter with better temperature regulation. The better ones we've tested all use a breathable construction to stop stuffy heat from pooling in the mattress, leading to overheating.

The Saatva Classic scored 5 out of 5 in our temperature regulation test, ranking just underneath our best cooling mattress of the year the Bear Elite Hybrid. With our tester lying on the bed, the Saatva's temperature crept up by just 6.3°F (compared to 7.3°F from the DreamCloud and 9°F on the Helix.) The Bear had a faster heat dissipation rate, shedding over eight degrees of heat in a minute compared to a 3°F shed from the Saatva.

At 1.12°F the DreamCloud had a faster dissipation rate than the Saatva Classic (1.26°F per minute), but it onboarded more heat: the DreamCloud had a Maximum Temperature Increase of 7.3°F, compared to 6.3°F on the Saatva and 9°F on the Helix. Subjective feedback from our testers was also mixed from the DreamCloud, with three out of five saying it felt warm to sleep on.

A mattress with good motion isolation can eat up movement from a restless partner, meaning you stand a better chance of sleeping peacefully through the night. But motion isolation is something even the best hybrid mattresses struggle with, as by design the layers of springs and coils add far more bounce to the bed than what you'd get from a memory foam mattress.

Industry observers note that we could see this 'bounce' during testing for all three mattresses. The Helix was best at absorbing initial force (just... it's impact rate of 7.4 is below the 7.8 and 7.9 of the Saatva and DreamCloud, respectively), as that thick, soft top eats up force.

But the Saatva Classic has the fastest decay rate at 1.703 — in under two seconds, movement came to a stop.

It has been revealed that strong edge support means you can lie on the side of your mattress without sliding off (a big deal for bed sharers). It also makes getting in and out of bed more comfortable, as you have a sturdy base to push against. We use a 25kg weight to assess the edge support on all mattresses we test.

The Saatva Classic has the best edge support of any bed we've come across. Foam railings deliver extra support to the sides, meaning our weight hardly sank (it showed 1" less sink at the foot of the bed than in the equivalent position on the Helix or DreamCloud).

Recent findings suggest that yes, you can sit and lie comfortable on both the DreamCloud Classic and the Helix Midnight Luxe... but you can park a truck on the edge of the Saatva.

Alongside our sleep lab, we test all mattresses at home for at least three weeks. The Saatva Classic, DreamCloud Classic Hybrid and Helix Midnight Luxe have all gone through extensive at-home testing over the past year.

During our Saatva Classic mattress review, our lead tester (and editor) described the Classic as having "the best pressure relief of any mattress we’ve reviewed so far.".

She noted that you lie on top of the surface while the materials contour to your body, a feel one member of our testing team called "weightless". Add on full-body support and a "gloriously cool-touch surface," and you have one of the best mattresses for back pain you can buy online.

According to recent reports, in comparison, our the DreamCloud Classic Hybrid mattress review team found it lacked a little lumbar support. However, our lead tester felt the bed "cushioned" her shoulders while "elevating" her spine, creating full-body comfort when side sleeping.

Recent findings suggest that this had a direct impact on her sleep quality; "I woke less in the night because I wasn’t tossing and turning as much," she explained. Lightweight back sleepers should also feel supported, although heavier members of our team noticed a slight "hamocking" effect.

Made for side sleepers, our Helix Midnight Luxe mattress review team felt it lived up to its promise with "incredible pressure relief to the shoulders and hips.".

It's also highly supportive for back sleepers, which is why our lead tester described it as the only mattress her and her husband have ever agreed on. The plush pillow-top delivers a "hug" that some find stifling — but others described as "cloud-like.".

In a recent development, right now is the best time to shop from all three brands. Saatva's sale is a step up from the Memorial Day offer, while DreamCloud's free gift sweetens an already excellent value boxed bed. We've seen slightly better from Helix... but we're talking a handful of dollars.

Recent findings suggest that in the Saatva Black Friday sale you can save $425 on all sizes of the Classic mattress, which is the biggest discount we've seen all year. A queen has dropped from $2,229 to $1,804 when you follow our links, while a twin is just $1,024 (was $1,449). A 365-night trial, lifetime warranty and free white glove delivery are included. You're unlikely to see a better Saatva mattress sale this year.

With a Classic Hybrid twin just $349 and a queen $699, the DreamCloud mattress sales are always good value. But this is a better deal than usual, with up to $898 worth of free bedding with every mattress in the DreamCloud Black Friday Sale. And you get a 365-night sleep trial plus a lifetime warranty.

It has been revealed that we've seen as much as 27% off the Midnight Luxe in the Helix mattress sales before but this 25% off deal is still an enticing offer — it drops a twin to $1,119 (was $1,492) and a queen to $1,874 (was $2,498.66). The Midnight Luxe comes with a 365-night trial and a lifetime warranty. For the biggest discount in the Helix Black Friday sale, consider upgrading to the Midnight Elite for 30% off.

Following our extensive lab and home testing, we recommend the Saatva Classic mattress to almost everyone. It's breathable, the edge support is impeccable and even the motion isolation is decent. With full-body support and an option for every sleep style, it's our number one pick overall.

But if you're a side sleeper and you want a mattress you sink into, try the Helix Midnight Luxe instead — the cushioning is luxurious and it eases hip and shoulder pain. And while the DreamCloud falls behind in lab results, it earned the title of our favorite mattress in a box because of it's sheer value. If you want a mattress under $1,000 that doesn't skimp on quality, this is the one.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Readdle updated its Documents app for iPhone and iPad this week with Voice Notes, a fresh AI-powered feature that lets customers record conversations and automatically generate transcripts, summaries, and follow-up notes. Here are the details.

While the habit of recording meetings, lectures, or even one’s own thoughts is not particularly new, modern AI tools and models have made it considerably easier to extract useful information from these recordings without having to listen back to them in their entirety or take copious notes that can distract from the actual conversation.

This week, Readdle’s Documents introduced Voice Notes, which “lets you record audio and turn it into a summary, follow-ups, and a full transcript,” as the manufacturer put it.

According to recent reports, users can start a latest recording session by tapping the “+” button in the app and selecting Voice Notes. Alternatively, they can start recording from the iPhone’s Action button, which is a nice touch.

Once they’re done, Readdle indicates Documents can generate:.

Owners can cycle through these three tabs, where they can also listen to the original recording or copy and share the information.

Readdle notes Voice Notes can recognize multiple languages in the same conversation, with the actual transcript preserving the languages as spoken, “while the summary and follow-ups are generated in the most frequently spoken language.”.

It has been revealed that each voice note is saved as a single file in Documents that contains the original recording, transcript, summary, and follow-ups. Consumers can organize these files into folders, share them, sync them with their cloud storage, and save the transcript as a separate .txt file.

However, if users give a voice note’s AI-generated content a thumbs down, Readdle may retain its transcript and summary for up to six months, or until the user objects to their processing, whichever comes first.

The firm also indicates user data isn’t used to train AI models, although third-party AI providers may retain inputs for up to 30 days for abuse and misuse monitoring, or longer if required by law.

To learn more about Voice Notes in Documents, follow this link.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple’s share of US smartphone shipments jumped from 50% to 57% year over year last quarter, with the manufacturer being the only major smartphone maker to buck the broader trend of declining shipments.
  • Sources indicate that yesterday, we covered a Counterpoint Research report on Q3 Latin American smartphone shipments, which indicated Apple recording the smallest year-over-year decline among the region’s top five smartphone makers.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple’s share of US smartphone shipments jumped from 50% to 57% year over year last quarter, with the manufacturer being the only major smartphone maker to buck the broader trend of declining shipments. Here are the details.

Sources indicate that yesterday, we covered a Counterpoint Research report on Q3 Latin American smartphone shipments, which indicated Apple recording the smallest year-over-year decline among the region’s top five smartphone makers. As a result, Apple increased its share of regional shipments from 7% to 9%.

The report echoed the findings of several others published throughout this year, which revealed how Apple has managed to navigate component shortages and rising costs better than many of its competitors, some of which have had to raise smartphone prices multiple times.

Apple, by contrast, kept iPhone pricing largely stable for much of the year, holding off on broader price increases until the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro lineup in September.

Today, Counterpoint Research released its report on US smartphone shipments for Q3, which indicated that Apple increased its share from 50% to 57% year over year, amid a 9% decline in overall shipments.

According to a separate Counterpoint report published last Thursday, Apple was the only major smartphone maker to avoid a year-over-year decline in shipment volume during the quarter.

In a recent development, in today’s report, Counterpoint notes that rising memory costs hit the low-end Android segment particularly hard during the quarter. Samsung was the only major Android smartphone maker to increase its shipment share, seeing a one-percentage-point bump to 25%, “helped by a portfolio spanning flagships and the low-end Galaxy A-series.”.

Carriers also felt the impact of the broader downturn, with smartphone sales across the three major US carriers collectively falling 4% year over year, per the report.

Looking ahead, Counterpoint expects memory costs to remain elevated and US carriers to be more selective with their holiday promotions, with smartphone sales expected to remain weak in Q4 despite it typically being the strongest quarter of the year.

South Korea proceeds with case over allegedly misleading Apple Intelligence ads

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (659 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, south Korea’s Fair Trade Commission (KFTC) announced today that it has opened formal proceedings against Apple over its advertising of Apple Intelligence features for the iPhone 16 lineup.
  • Back in March 2025, shortly after Apple declared it was delaying the rollout of what would eventually become Siri AI, the South Korean civic group Seoul YMCA filed a complaint with the KFTC.
  • At the time, Yonhap reported that the organization had previously called on Apple to compensate affected customers, and alleged that the firm may have continued to market the iPhone 16 lineup despite already knowing that some of its advertised AI features would be delayed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, south Korea’s Fair Trade Commission (KFTC) announced today that it has opened formal proceedings against Apple over its advertising of Apple Intelligence features for the iPhone 16 lineup. Here are the details.

Back in March 2025, shortly after Apple declared it was delaying the rollout of what would eventually become Siri AI, the South Korean civic group Seoul YMCA filed a complaint with the KFTC.

At the time, Yonhap reported that the organization had previously called on Apple to compensate affected customers, and alleged that the firm may have continued to market the iPhone 16 lineup despite already knowing that some of its advertised AI features would be delayed.

As 9to5Mac readers will likely remember, Apple widely advertised Apple Intelligence and AI-powered Siri features as part of its iPhone 16 launch campaign, going so far as to give its iconic Fifth Avenue store an Apple Intelligence-themed makeover and run an ad campaign starring Bella Ramsey.

According to recent reports, this landed Apple in legal and regulatory trouble in multiple markets, including the US, where the manufacturer agreed to a $250 million class action settlement earlier this year, and Brazil, where it came under scrutiny from a consumer protection agency in May. Now, the company is facing potential penalties in South Korea as well.

As a result of Seoul YMCA’s complaint, the KFTC conducted an investigation into Apple’s advertising practices. Today, the regulator announced (via MacRumors) that its investigators had submitted their findings and recommendations for formal deliberation by the Commission.

According to the KFTC’s press release, investigators concluded that Apple advertised Apple Intelligence and its planned staggered rollout on the iPhone 16 website, but “concealed, downplayed, or omitted information material to consumers’ purchasing decisions.”.

That included, per the press release (translation ours):.

The press release also notes that Genmoji, Image Playground, “Siri with the ability to understand personal context,” and “Siri that provides step-by-step guidance” were not made available as advertised:.

For example, Siri’s ability to understand personal context was advertised as being scheduled to launch first in US English by the end of 2024, as currently available in US English in October 2024, and as scheduled to support Korean in early April 2025.

In reality, the feature was not launched in US English until September 2026, with Korean language support following in October 2026.

As a result, the investigators concluded that Apple’s conduct constituted a violation of the country’s Labeling and Advertising Act, which prohibits deceptive labeling and advertising.

They recommended issuing corrective orders, including a prohibition on such conduct in the future, as well as imposing a financial penalty.

They also estimate that Apple’s revenue associated with the alleged violation amounts to approximately 3.35 trillion South Korean won (roughly $2.5 billion), though the KFTC’s press release does not specify the amount of the fine.

⁠Yonhap noted today that the fine could reach roughly $48 million, while ⁠KBS reported that it could range between $21 million and $42 million.

With the report now submitted, Apple has six weeks to submit its written defense before the Commission deliberates and makes a final determination on whether the manufacturer violated the law and, if so, how much it should be fined.

In a statement to MacRumors, Apple said it had cooperated with the KFTC’s investigation, but disagreed with the conclusions. The manufacturer also highlighted the rollout of Korean-language support for Apple Intelligence last year and, more recently, for Siri AI.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Uncertainty in the Middle East, elevated Treasury yields and fears about an AI bubble continue to keep global markets on edge. Given this volatile backdrop, investors seeking stable income can consider enhancing their portfolios by adding dividend-paying stocks.

However, the vast universe of dividend stocks can make selection challenging. Tracking the ratings of top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend stocks, as their recommendations are backed by in-depth research.

Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Chord Energy is an independent exploration and production organization with long-lived assets primarily in the Williston Basin. With a quarterly base dividend of $1.30 per share, CHRD offers a dividend yield of 3.67%.

According to recent reports, in a research note on third-quarter expectations, RBC Capital analyst Scott Hanold reiterated a buy rating on CHRD stock with a price target of $175. "We model production near the top of guidance and continue to see strong performance from new wells and base production," mentioned Hanold.

According to recent reports, specifically, the five-star analyst expects Q3 2026 production at 283 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day, or Mboe/d, in line with the Street's consensus and near the high end of the 278 to 284 Mboe/d guidance. Hanold said his Q3 2026 earnings per share estimate increased to $5.29 due to lower non-cash depreciation, depletion and amortization.

Meanwhile, cash flow per share estimate moved lower to $13.59 to reflect Hanold's update based on the current backdrop and commodity mark-to-market. He expects Chord Energy to report capital spending of $375 million for Q3 2026, slightly above the Street's estimate of $369 million.

Overall, Hanold remains bullish on CHRD, given its best-in-class balance sheet. He expects a free cash flow payout of 80% in the third quarter, with the possibility of an upside. Hanold expects investors to focus on management commentary on 2027 capital plans, Williston M&A opportunities, and long-term performance of 4-mile wells.

Hanold ranks No. 310 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 14.9%. See Chord Energy KPIs on TipRanks.

Williams, an energy infrastructure firm that delivers natural gas, is the next dividend pick. The company recently completed the $5.5 billion acquisition of Momentum Midstream, which will expand its natural gas infrastructure in the Haynesville to meet growing Gulf Coast LNG, power and industrial demand. At a quarterly dividend of $0.5250 per share, Williams offers a yield of 2.89%.

In her latest research note, RBC Capital analyst Elvira Scotto reiterated a buy rating on Williams stock with a price target of $87. Ahead of Q3 2026 earnings, the analyst remarked that she expects WMB to announce strong quarterly performance.

Sources indicate that scotto raised her estimates to reflect insights from the quarterly catch-up call, the completion of the Momentum Midstream acquisition, and mark-to-market quarter-to-date commodity prices. She expects WMB to report Q3 2026 adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of $2,036 million, which is modestly above the Street's consensus estimate.

Furthermore, Scotto expects Williams' Transmission, Power & Gulf segment to increase quarter-over-quarter, driven by the startup of the Socrates power project and favorable natural gas liquids, or NGL, margins.

In a recent development, scotto noted that WMB stock has underperformed due to backlash related to data centers and investor anticipation of another Power Innovation project. She expects the company to announce at least one more project before the end of this year, potentially with a newly introduced customer and a contract duration of 15 to 20 years, which would be a positive catalyst for the stock.

Scotto ranks No. 175 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been profitable 67% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.2%. See Williams Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

Industry observers note that EOG Resources, a crude oil and natural gas exploration and production organization, will hold its third-quarter earnings call on Nov. 6. At a quarterly dividend of $1.02 per share, EOG offers a dividend yield of 2.75%.

It has been revealed that heading into Q3 earnings, Jefferies analyst Lloyd Byrne reiterated a buy rating on EOG Resources stock and increased his price target to $185 from $175. The analyst expects the company's Q3 cash flow per share to exceed the Street's consensus by 13%, driven by better-than-expected production.

Byrne expects crude oil production, excluding the UAE, to reach 551 Mboe/d, which is at the high end of guidance (546-551 Mboe/d) and above the Street's projection of 548 Mboe/d, driven by continued growth in the Utica.

Furthermore, Byrne expects cash operating expenses to come in at $10.27 per barrel of oil equivalent, below the midpoint of guidance of $10.05 to $11.35, helped by lower lease operating expenses. Overall, the analyst expects EOG to deliver free cash flow of $2.65 billion, supporting another quarter of buybacks near the minimum 70% shareholder return threshold and implying about $1.5 billion in share repurchases.

"As a first indication of the '27 plan, we expect EOG will message another year of mid-single-digit (~3.5%) growth on a flat capital budget (~$6.55bn), which is above the Street modeling 1% oil growth at $6.6bn," said Byrne.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption. Microsoft has just put its offering into the ring.

During the keynote for the firm’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella announced Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.

Also: Microsoft says its fresh AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.

The product, available in Frontier for now, is similar to OpenAI’s ChatGPT Space and several new Anthropic features, including Whiteboard and Sheets, which essentially merge the work tools you’re used to using with an agentic framework.

“As the evolution of Copilot Notebooks, it’s where people and agents build on each other’s work,” Microsoft said. “An agent drafts a section of a document, and you review. You leave a comment, and an agent picks it up.”.

Microsoft also unveiled Autopilot, a sort of counterpoint agent to Copilot that “can watch Teams channels, follow up on emails, run recurring work, and manage a project — without waiting for a prompt,” as Microsoft described.

In a demo video during the keynote, the agent appeared to function similarly to OpenAI’s Dots, but for work — employees can tag their Autopilot “like a colleague,” Microsoft said, and assign it tasks.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s fresh Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.

Microsoft noted the agent will be able to autonomously handle “meetings and follow-ups on its own,” though that claim may be best verified by teams themselves.

Speaking of trust, however, Microsoft noted that “Autopilot runs on the identity, security, and compliance foundation IT already uses,” and that “each Autopilot has its own Microsoft Entra Agent ID and a named manager,” meaning IT can block it as needed.

“Its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, so security teams have a clear audit trail. Powered by Work IQ, it understands how your organization works within existing permissions,” Microsoft remarked.

Sources indicate that the organization added that employees will soon “be able to bring their personal Autopilot into Workspaces” as well. The feature is also available in Frontier.

According to recent reports, nadella also announced a few other productivity features, including a “command center” called Today that spans email, calendar, meetings, tasks, and threads in Teams. Currently in private preview in Outlook and the Copilot app, it includes a personalized briefing and a feed of priorities that updates throughout the day.

“The draft is written and ready for you to edit; the schedule change is already proposed; and the forgotten follow-up is waiting for you to send it, complete with context so you can catch up promptly,” Microsoft said of the feature, which sounds like an agentic briefing-cum-morning-assistant.

Also: Nearly 70% of workers use AI regularly now – but many get no time to upskill.

In a recent development, microsoft also announced that Home, now generally available, unifies Chat and Cowork into a singular starting point. That’s similar to Anthropic’s recent consolidation of its chat and agentic Cowork offerings, demonstrating an overall trend toward simplification in workplace AI.

While more companies are finally starting to see a return on their AI investment, agents are still expensive and can rapidly rack up costs when unsupervised.

Microsoft declared a few tools to track this at Ignite: Agent 365 Business Analytics and Agent 365 Cost Management.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Sources indicate that agent 365, which Microsoft announced last year, is the manufacturer’s observability platform. Microsoft said Business Analytics, in Frontier Public today, provides insights on what a company is spending on AI and why, and where it’s paying off, as well as forecasts future costs. In a demo during the keynote, Microsoft showed how admins can see when specific agents’ costs have spiked recently and what (human) employee to notify as a result.

“It starts with a new way to measure your investment: in work completed, not simply tokens,” Microsoft remarked. “It analyzes the tasks, how long that work typically takes a person, and the share Cowork performed, providing a sophisticated view of the hours your intelligence supports and what the work is worth.”.

Cost Management lets IT see where teams are using AI down to the model.

“Leaders can set spending policies, limits, and proactive alerts and control which models are available,” Microsoft said. Anthropic released a similar tool last month, though it was focused more on making seats as efficient as possible on Teams and Enterprise plans.

  • MAI remarked it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, during the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella revealed several new models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the tech giant. But new model releases are almost a dime a dozen these days, and accelerating fast — what really stood out was how Microsoft will let its customers access those models.

Also: Microsoft indicates its newly introduced AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.

MAI remarked it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights. It’s essentially a selective approach to open-weight AI: more so than proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic, but not fully downloadable on Hugging Face like Mistral’s Le Chonk. Interested companies will need to go through their Microsoft account reps to get started.

In a recent development, “You control who can access it. Your data and adaptations stay entirely yours. And we’ll work with you through Frontier Tech giant to deliver the custom model and embed it in your own products and agents,” Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of MAI, stated during the keynote.

It has been revealed that the approach should stand out to businesses looking for affordable AI that lets them retain control over their IP. Microsoft said it would only use customers’ information to train its models if they agreed.

“No one wants to pour their IQ into someone else’s model,” Suleyman remarked during the keynote, a nod to an argument Palantir CEO Alex Karp has made repeatedly.

According to recent reports, the dominant, if simplified, narrative in AI has been that proprietary, expensive models boast peak capabilities but aren’t customizable, while open, cheaper models are customizable but less capable. Microsoft’s AI models don’t necessarily compete with OpenAI and Anthropic yet, but the company has legacy sway with countless businesses. By offering a customizable AI option, it could strike a balance among major tech companies.

According to recent reports, western labs, including Thinking Machines and Mistral, are releasing more competitive open-weight models, but Anthropic and OpenAI still have the overwhelming majority of the enterprise AI market. Though Licensed Weights isn’t an open-weight family of models, it does diversify the open-versus-closed debate a bit and differentiate Microsoft’s offering from OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s. It’s also a smart pairing with Microsoft’s goal to balance price and performance, if businesses find it impressive enough.

Also: Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026.

“Averaged over four widely used benchmarks that target the everyday enterprise coding tasks we see in GitHub Copilot, MAI Code 2 gives you 98% of the performance of GPT 6.1 Sol at just 40% of the cost, and against Opus 5.5 it’s an incredible 5% of that cost,” Suleyman noted of the upcoming coding model the tech giant revealed at Ignite.

The company also released its latest image editing model, MAI Image 2.7, on Tuesday, which now leads the category on Artificial Analysis while beating Nano Banana Pro and several GPT image models on price and quality. With Licensed Weights, Microsoft has positioned itself for organizations seeking a reliable blend of ROI tools, customization, security controls, and capability.

SpaceX Sued by 2 States Over Grok’s Sexualized Images of Women and Children

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Oregon and Virginia on Monday filed lawsuits against SpaceX, alleging that Elon Musk’s tech giant violated consumer protection laws, months after people used Grok Imagine to generate millions of sexualized images of women and children.
  • Grok Imagine is an image- and video-generation tool developed by SpaceXSI, a division of SpaceX.
  • In the lawsuits, separate but jointly filed, Virginia and Oregon allege that the sexualized images — including child sexual abuse material — were generated without the knowledge and consent of the women and children shown in the images and videos.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Oregon and Virginia on Monday filed lawsuits against SpaceX, alleging that Elon Musk’s tech giant violated consumer protection laws, months after people used Grok Imagine to generate millions of sexualized images of women and children.

Grok Imagine is an image- and video-generation tool developed by SpaceXSI, a division of SpaceX. Shortly after launching last summer, the tool added a “spicy mode,” which enabled people to generate images and videos showing partial nudity and adult-themed videos. Grok Imagine is integrated into Grok, which is Musk’s AI chatbot.

In the lawsuits, separate but jointly filed, Virginia and Oregon allege that the sexualized images — including child sexual abuse material — were generated without the knowledge and consent of the women and children shown in the images and videos.

Read more: After Rampant AI-Powered Abuse, Grok Doubles Down.

Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones stated in a press release that SpaceX misled people into thinking that their images and data would be safe.

“When xAI [now renamed SpaceXSI] allowed Grok’s creators to sideline consent to turn a profit, they prioritized growth and engagement over safety, and they deceived the public about it,” Jones noted. “Today’s filings are the first step towards holding this organization accountable.”.

Donna Rice Hughes, CEO of child internet safety organization Enough Is Enough, praised Oregon and Virginia for taking action against SpaceX.

“It is abhorrent that women and children are preyed upon in this manner and even more repugnant that xAI’s Grok ‘spicy mode’ has not kept up with bad actors who abuse their terms of service,” Hughes told CNET, adding that Musk’s “team can find ways to prevent criminal misuse of Grok, and at the very least, disable Grok’s ‘spicy mode.'”.

Grok Imagine debuted on Aug. 5, 2025, and within months, it was used to generate millions of sexualized images, which were posted on the social media platform X, which is also owned by Musk’s SpaceX.

Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield alleged SpaceX “knowingly designed” Grok Imagine and promoted spicy mode’s lack of safeguards as a feature, not a bug.

According to recent reports, “It’s no surprise that Grok and X became a haven for perpetrators using AI to create and share child sexual abuse material,” Rayfield noted in a statement. “The lack of needed safety measures was considered a feature, not a bug, which they promoted as ‘spicy mode.’”.

During a 9-day span starting in late December, Grok posted about 3 million sexualized images, according to an analysis from the Center for Countering Digital Hate.

Sources indicate that in a statement posted Monday on X, SpaceX said that people using Grok to generate sexualized images and videos violated the platform’s terms of service and worked “aggressively to circumvent our safeguards.” The manufacturer said it tightened protections after the misuse and continues to test and adjust them as needed. SpaceX also said it notifies law enforcement authorities “when someone tries to break our safeguards and generate this content.”.

Earlier this year, several minor Jane Does filed a proposed class action lawsuit against xAI after people used their photos to generate child sexual abuse material using Grok via spicy mode. That case is still ongoing.

According to recent reports, in July, a victim’s family also filed suit after photographer Russell Bloodworth in Arkansas allegedly used spicy mode to generate explicit photos of children. xAI went on the offensive, suing Bloodworth and South Carolina man Terry Wayne Harwood, who is also accused of using Grok to generate child sexual abuse material. The company seeks damages for expenses incurred in fighting lawsuits and for reputational harm.

Recent findings suggest that spaceX and xAI have faced lawsuits for other things aside from illicit image generation. The companies were sued for allegedly sharing sensitive data and for allegedly causing users to be hospitalized for psychosis after harmful chat conversations on Grok.

Monday’s lawsuits against SpaceX are among nearly 400 cases brought against 129 AI companies in the US, according to the AI Lawsuit Tracker. Many Substantial Tech companies have been sued for allegedly harming the mental health of adults and children. In August, Meta agreed to pay $18 billion to settle a lawsuit brought by US states alleging the manufacturer intentionally designed Instagram and other platforms to be addictive to children.

Companies such as ByteDance — owner of TikTok — Snap, Google and others face more than 2,400 federal lawsuits alleging that their platforms harm the mental health of children.

According to recent reports, ubuntu 27.04, Tenacious T-Rex, is set for an April 22, 2027 release. Although that seems a long way off, it’s sooner than you think. As is implied by the release number, 27.04 is not an LTS release, so it only receives support for nine months (until January 2028). The good news is that you can migrate from 27.04 to 27.10, and then to the LTS release, 28.04. The entire upgrade path ensures that you don’t have to miss a single release.

In a recent development, but what’s coming in Ubuntu 27.04? Given that it’s an interim release, you’re probably assuming that there’ll be nothing exciting to be found. Although there won’t be any game-changing additions, there will be plenty of refinements and bug fixes.

Also: I’ve used Ubuntu for 22 years – and 26.10 might be its best release yet.

Industry observers note that I’ve been using the daily release of Ubuntu 27.04 for a bit. Let’s take a look at what is currently expected in Tenacious T-Rex.

Industry observers note that this is probably the biggest addition to the next release of Ubuntu. And although you won’t find any major changes in GNOME, there are some notable ones. First off, there will be editable quick settings, which allow for customizing, adding, removing, and rearranging toggles and widgets. GNOME 52 will also enjoy a revamped calendar popover, which streamlines the feature to focus primarily on events, time, and weather.

Also: Over Ubuntu? Fedora is the Linux distro I’d hop to next – here’s why.

There will also be several improvements to window management, such as a spatial overview and a mosaic/tiling system for auto-resizing and organizing windows, a refined full-screen Alt+Tab app switcher, which will be capable of grouping older windows by application while showing newer ones individually, and finally, the ability to remember window sizing, placement, and workspace.

It has been revealed that desktop search is also getting a bit of polish by way of a redesigned popover and an improved results overlay that includes file previews, multiple actions, and search filters. And, as usual, there will be plenty of bug fixes and performance enhancements. The bump in speed is noticeable, too, in my testing.

Ubuntu 27.04 will ship with the Linux 7.6 kernel, which includes better VRAM management for gaming and expanded support for modern hardware, such as early enablement for AMD Zen 6, stable support for Intel Xe3P, mainline boot capabilities for Apple M3 Pro/Max/Ultra, and initial support for the 2026 Steam Controller.

There will also be performance gains for both the Btrfs and Ext4 file systems, which (along with the improvements in GNOME 52) will make Ubuntu 27.04 one of the best-performing releases in some time.

Also: This lightweight Linux distro revives old PCs destined for the junk pile – and it’s beautiful.

I will say this: I’ve come to count on Ubuntu’s latest releases to be an improvement over the previous iterations, and from what I’ve seen so far in my testing, 27.04 will not disappoint. Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

On a sobering evening for new Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

Recent findings suggest that among the Newcastle players introduced at half-time was 18-year-old Sean Steur, the exciting midfield prospect signed from Ajax this summer. Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure also flickered with promise, but a sharp start from Jaissle’s team faded.

They pulled a goal back late on when Jacob Murphy’s cross found Harvey Barnes at the back post, but they offered little as an attacking force throughout the second half.

Newcastle have two more friendlies, against Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg, before they begin their Premier League season at home to Liverpool.

The club are reeling from the summer departures of Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe, but David Hopkinson, the chief executive, struck a bullish tone when he spoke of this being the start of “Newcastle 2.0”.

Everton look the more settled side and club, and the performances of newly introduced arrivals Hackney and George were encouraging, while Thierno Barry was sharp in the centre-forward position that has proved so difficult for the club to fill in recent seasons.

Everton kick-off their new season at home to Crystal Palace, and keeping Ndiaye at the club beyond the end of the transfer window will be a priority.

Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the latest season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

Recent findings suggest that “We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”.

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

Sources indicate that “Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”.

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he mentioned.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”.

Uber Riders Can Now Request to Have Their Trips Recorded

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (549 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that starting this week, Uber riders in select markets will be able to specify that they want their trip recorded on video.
  • Recent findings suggest that after a series of rider safety investigations and sexual assault lawsuit settlements, Uber began looking for ways to boost passenger safety and confidence in the service.
  • According to Uber, the knowledge that a trip is being recorded gives both riders and drivers peace of mind.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that starting this week, Uber riders in select markets will be able to specify that they want their trip recorded on video. The feature, which is being introduced in Baltimore, Indianapolis, St. Louis, and Raleigh, North Carolina, adds a new Recorded Rides choice to the app alongside other familiar ride options like UberX and UberXL. Uber claims that the new feature gives “greater confidence that a recording will be there if something doesn’t go as planned.”.

Recent findings suggest that after a series of rider safety investigations and sexual assault lawsuit settlements, Uber began looking for ways to boost passenger safety and confidence in the service. The ridesharing platform first tested in-app trip audio recording in late 2019, then piloted the Record My Ride feature in 2022, before finally rolling out the video recording function in earnest, first in San Francisco in 2023, then nationally across the US in 2024.

According to Uber, the knowledge that a trip is being recorded gives both riders and drivers peace of mind.

While drivers can opt out of using the feature in their settings, more than half of its active drivers in the US choose to record their trips in the Record My Ride feature.

Starting this week, Uber riders in those four cities will be able to request a recorded ride during the hailing process in the Uber app and, when possible, be automatically matched with a driver using the feature. Choosing a recorded ride doesn’t affect the fare.

Record My Ride has been available to Uber’s drivers, though not passengers, for a few years now. The feature uses the front-facing camera on the driver’s phone to capture trip audio and video.

Uber says the recordings are encrypted and stored on the driver’s device to protect the privacy of drivers and riders, and are automatically deleted after a period of time.

“Uber can only review recordings uploaded as part of a safety report or insurance claim,” a representative told CNET.

Not selecting a Recorded Ride doesn’t guarantee that your trip won’t be recorded in some way. Many Uber drivers choose to install separate dash cams in their vehicles, often with multiple cameras recording into the cabin. Uber offers drivers the option to register their dash cam with the service, but this is separate from the pilot.

“Drivers can use a separate dash cam, provided they comply with local laws,” an Uber representative told CNET in an email, “but Recorded Rides specifically matches riders with drivers recording through Record My Ride.”.

Recent findings suggest that uber says it’s exploring additional ways to use recordings to keep its riders and drivers safe. It will soon begin proactively activating the Record My Ride feature on drivers’ devices during trips that may benefit from additional oversight, such as late-night or trips involving teenagers. Uber is also looking into automatically turning on video recordings “when trips are not proceeding as expected,” such as when a trip goes significantly off the projected course or if a crash is detected.

Industry observers note that uber says it’s also looking into testing the automatic activation of audio recording on riders’ phones during nighttime trips. Passengers would have to consent to this, which would require the app to use their phone’s microphone.
