  • According to a Reuters investigation, Meta employees testing Muse remarked the agent messaged them about topics they hadn’t asked it about, including career advice, a follow-up on a request for childcare, products they hadn’t purchased, and, crucially, bank account balances they didn’t recognize.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Meta’s Muse AI agent has only been around for a few months, but already has a track record of user privacy violations. Even Meta employees are reporting concerning incidents, including the agent taking actions they didn’t ask it to and sharing information they didn’t recognize that appears to belong to other users.

Recent findings suggest that also: Don’t use Muse? Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages.

According to a Reuters investigation, Meta employees testing Muse remarked the agent messaged them about topics they hadn’t asked it about, including career advice, a follow-up on a request for childcare, products they hadn’t purchased, and, crucially, bank account balances they didn’t recognize.

These incidents “prompted unnerved employees to raise concerns it could be mixing up conversations between different accounts and exposing people’ private data,” Reuters said.

Reuters stated “an employee told colleagues his Muse had randomly added an extra message to its regular chats about fishing-related weather and tide information, saying: ‘BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2,722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5,899.57.'” In another instance, Muse booked a non-refundable Airbnb for an employee who hadn’t instructed it to.

Muse notified another employee, who was using the agent on her personal phone, about a message she’d received on Signal, though she said she hadn’t given the agent access to the encrypted messaging app.

Also: Meta Muse is the worst AI agent for privacy – and I’ve tried them all.

Reuters and the AI Now Institute determined, through testing on an Android phone and a Mac, that Muse used “permissions granted during the bot’s initial setup to pull in the message text, leveraging those authorizations in ways a user might not anticipate.” Because Muse is set up with automatic access to Android push notifications, it didn’t need explicit app access to read messages.

The tests did not work on an iPhone, suggesting better protections against Muse’s prying.

It has been revealed that similarly, in September, a user reported Muse had shared his address with a Facebook Marketplace buyer before checking with him. The incident was ultimately a misunderstanding between the terms the user thought he’d consented to and how much access he was actually handing over, which exemplifies that Meta and the user may have explicitly different definitions of access, and that Muse can take advantage of that grey area.

Meta told Reuters these incidents were either isolated or the result of hallucinations, though Reuters could not confirm that.

According to recent reports, these are just the latest in a string of alarming incidents surrounding Muse. In its first month, a cybersecurity professional discovered Muse had a serious zero-day bug that made it hijackable. At least one journalist found the AI sifting through his Apple Messages after he’d explicitly denied those permissions, which Apple then issued stronger privacy protections to address. Banks have also blocked agents over concerns.

Recent findings suggest that as a company, Meta doesn’t have a solid history of respecting user privacy. That legacy is partly what informed ZDNET contributor David Gewirtz’s suspicion of the AI assistant when he tested it, though it earned his assigned title of “worst AI agent for privacy” all on its own. The agent asked him for everything from contacts and chats to his logins and passwords, and Meta automatically uses conversations with Muse to train its AI.

Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac.

Public awareness of the risks of AI agents hit a peak last year with the viral OpenClaw. The predominant advice for using agents has been to take every privacy precaution: Be careful with the data you share and the apps you give it permissions for, and watch what you tell it. But if users believe they’re doing so by restricting access to certain apps, just for Muse to find a way in anyway, privacy hygiene isn’t enough.

Also: How to keep your chatbot conversations as private as possible.

Reuters’ findings may provide an opportunity for Google’s agentic offering, now called Tasks (formerly Spark), which it made free (with usage limits, like Muse) this week.

#143701. Breaking: This Is What My Apple Watch Heard When I Let It Evesdrop on My Conversations

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1228 w)

Breaking: This Is What My Apple Watch Heard When I Let It Evesdrop on My Conversations

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1228 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • No, your phone isn’t listening to you.
  • Along with the general sensor, processor, and battery upgrades, the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 introduced Audio Intelligence, a latest set of features that allows the watch to listen in on conversations.
  • Siri Recap generates summaries of what you’ve discussed throughout the day, while Live Rewind gives you a transcript of the last 15 seconds of audio in case you missed something.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

No, your phone isn’t listening to you. But what about your Apple Watch? I’ve been testing new Audio Intelligence features that record conversations around me, and despite how disturbing it may sound to have your smartwatch listening and taking notes of your entire day, the reality has been a lot more mundane.

Along with the general sensor, processor, and battery upgrades, the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 introduced Audio Intelligence, a latest set of features that allows the watch to listen in on conversations.

Siri Recap generates summaries of what you’ve discussed throughout the day, while Live Rewind gives you a transcript of the last 15 seconds of audio in case you missed something.

It’s similar functionality as AI-powered recording pins like Plaud or Amazon’s Bee, but within the context of your smartwatch and without the additional cost or subscription.

And it’s completely optional. You have to first opt-in to the features to activate them, then choose to turn the feature you want on whenever you want to start using it. Then you can leave it on all day, set it on a schedule or toggle it manually whenever you need it. If you’re like me and forget that it’s on, you get reminders that it’s still listening or to check your recaps.

The fact that you have so much control over whether you use it and how much helped ease the creepy factor for me, but there’s still everyone else to consider.

According to recent reports, beyond a barely audible chime when I double-click the Digital Crown to activate Live Rewind, there’s no way to alert others that the feature is in use and that whoever’s in earshot is inadvertently getting roped into my little experiment as well. Other wearables like smart glasses have an indicator light on the front to alert spectators when they’re recording video.

Apple has built-in privacy safeguards for the audio, how it’s processed and then deleted. I’ve broken all that down in a separate Audio Intelligence FAQ. This is about what it’s like to use it in the wild.

According to recent reports, I’ve been testing Audio Intelligence in the WatchOS 27.3 (and iOS) public beta for two weeks. Because this isn’t the final version (Apple indicates it will release publicly later this year), consider this a sneak preview.

Recent findings suggest that let’s get Live Rewind out of the way because there’s not a lot to say about it. Whether from a lack of muscle memory (or usefulness), I’ve had to go out of my way to remember the feature exists.

I figured it’d come in handy for those “come again?” moments during conversations, but the reality is that it’s just easier to ask someone to repeat what they mentioned than remember to double-press the Digital Crown at just the right moment. I can see it being more useful when you’re listening to a presentation or other event.

According to recent reports, fifteen seconds go by a lot faster than I expect and by the time I realize something might be worth revisiting, the person has moved on with the conversation. I either missed what I intended to get or just captured the silence after.

Siri Recap has been more useful, though it’s still hit-or-miss. The feature gives you high-level summaries of what it heard — it doesn’t provide a transcript to review, and it doesn’t identify who noted what. It shines brightest during dedicated meetings when there’s a single conversation to follow rather than a jumble of unrelated discussions.

One success story: I was moderating the chat for our iPhone Duo live folding test on YouTube while Matthew Murray, CNET’s lab director, answered viewer questions on the stream.

I thought I’d caught the gist of what he was saying, but the typing must’ve distracted me more than I realized because I was pleasantly surprised to learn some interesting facts that I’d missed in the Siri Recap, like “Opening a phone 20 times daily over 10 years equals 73,000 folds” or that the “machine runs approximately 22,560 cycles every 24 hours”.

According to recent reports, but Siri’s batting average wasn’t always that good, which made it challenging to trust the notes. During a conversation with another mom about car-pool logistics, Siri Recap pulled out action items, like who I was picking up and at what time, which I appreciated, but the information wasn’t accurate. Not only had Siri gotten the names of the kids wrong, it also had me picking up the wrong kid. Clearly, the mental load of figuring out after-school logistics is challenging even for Siri.

Siri can’t handle the messy conversations (and TV shows).

Where things get interesting (and occasionally hilarious) is how Siri discerns what constitutes a conversation and how many topics belong in a single recap.

Siri is generally good at accurately labeling what conversations are about: “Parent-teacher conferences,” “Car-pool logistics,” “Folding phone durability testing.” But rather than keeping them separate, as it should, it sometimes conflates two or even three completely unrelated conversations into a single recap.

Sources indicate that I encountered bullet points summarizing a serious conversation with a friend about a medical condition alongside notes about a chaotic (albeit funny) exploding apple cider incident with my kids. The two conversations happened within the same two-hour window, but they were by no means back-to-back.

It’s a good thing Siri Recap leaves out tone and volume cause that last bullet would’ve been in ALL CAPS.

Recent findings suggest that what it did decide was worthy of a standalone recap was a discussion about wedding plans during an episode of Nobody Wants This on Netflix. To be fair, this would’ve absolutely warranted a recap if I’d been discussing my own wedding plans; however, the fact that the “conversation” happened at midnight should’ve tipped off Siri that this was a late-night binge session and not an actual conversation needing to be recapped.

According to recent reports, rather than coming away better informed about the crucial conversations I’d had throughout the day, I came away feeling validated by the sheer chaos of it all. The constant whiplash of being pulled in a dozen different directions — bouncing between work, kids, gossip and the occasional sticky beverage crisis — was real and now immortalized (until the recap automatically expires if you don’t choose to save it).

For now, while novel, neither Siri Recap nor Live Rewind is reason enough to buy (or avoid) the Apple Watch Series 12 or Ultra 4. They’re two of our top-rated smartwatches for their fitness, health and other smart features. Audio Intelligence is either an added bonus (it’s free) or something you can ignore altogether.

But if you do decide to venture into this brave upcoming world of AI notetakers, my suggestion would be to use Siri Recap intentionally rather than leaving it running all day.

It has been revealed that turn it on before a work meeting, a doctor’s appointment or another conversation where you might want a few notes to jog your memory later. Just make sure everyone involved knows it’s enabled and is comfortable with it, and that you’re not relying on it for crucial information.

If the stakes are high, have a backup — whether that’s your own notes or a recording — lest you risk coming home with the wrong kid.

By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 26, 2026 at 2:05PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Johnson & Johnson ›.

Recent findings suggest that johnson & Johnson (JNJ -0.91%) and Procter & Gamble (PG +0.44%) sell products that are bought in both good times and bad. That's notable right now because the so-called Buffett indicator is more than two standard deviations above its historical average, suggesting a high risk of a downturn. If you are a conservative investor, safe-haven stocks in the healthcare and consumer staples sectors should be high on your wish list. Here's why.

Sources indicate that warren Buffett was the former CEO of Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA +0.54%)(BRKB +0.37%). His long-term investment approach resulted in the tech giant achieving incredible long-term returns for investors. A key piece of the story was his penchant for waiting to buy until stock prices were attractive. That meant holding off during periods of overvaluation. The tool he used to determine the valuation of the broader market was the total value of the stock market divided by gross domestic product (GDP).

Recent findings suggest that it is a rough gauge, at best. But when the Buffett indicator is at an extreme level, as it is today, it's worth taking a step back. You may want to reevaluate your portfolio, perhaps holding more cash. Or, if you want to remain invested, increasing your exposure to more conservative dividend stocks that have a history of holding up during periods of economic and market weakness. That's exactly what you'll find with J&J and P&G.

One of the big reasons to like J&J right now is that it is a Dividend King, with the longest dividend streak of any healthcare company at 64 years. It has successfully navigated multiple recessions and bear markets over that span. While the company has changed over the years, it presently focuses on the pharmaceutical and medical device segments of the broader healthcare sector.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

The big story is that drugs and medical devices usually aren't optional purchases. Consumers are willing to pay for them because they improve their lives and can sometimes mean the difference between life and death. That makes J&J very resilient, a fact bolstered by its diversification across two business lines.

Sources indicate that the one problem is valuation. J&J isn't cheap right now, but for conservative investors, it may be worth paying a premium if the lofty level of the Buffett indicator has you worried. That mentioned, the healthcare giant's 1.9% dividend yield is well above the 1% you'd collect from the S&P 500 index (^GSPC -0.25%) and the healthcare average of roughly 1.3%.

P&G is one of the world's largest consumer staples companies. It has a strong brand portfolio focused on paper products, toiletries, and makeup. Most of its products sit at the high end of their categories, which would seem like a risky place to be during an economic downturn. However, P&G has long focused on innovation, producing products that consumers are willing to pay more for. Notably, despite belt-tightening in many households today, P&G's organic sales grew 4% in the first quarter of fiscal 2027.

And consumers aren't likely to stop buying their favorite toilet paper and toothpaste even if there is a downturn. At least that's what history has shown, helping P&G to increase its dividend for 70 consecutive years. Like J&J, that's the best streak in its peer group.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

According to recent reports, P&G isn't exactly cheap, either. However, its price-to-sales and price-to-earnings ratios are roughly in line with their five-year averages. That suggests the stock is fairly valued right now. And the stock's 2.5% yield is above the consumer staples average of 2%, so you are getting a generous yield.

Recent findings suggest that the Buffett indicator is flashing bright red warning signs right now, given its elevated level. If that has you thinking about dialing back on risk, you should consider reliable dividend stocks from defensive sectors like healthcare and consumer staples. The best dividend records in those two sectors belong to Johnson & Johnson and Procter & Gamble. It's probably a good idea to start your search with these two safe-haven stocks.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

Sources indicate that emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the big positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

According to recent reports, signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the fresh year.

Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj.

His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”.

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

Industry observers note that while some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Sources indicate that hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx.

It was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

Before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

Brian Madjo with a significant chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15.

PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr.

Villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

It became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

PSG (4-3-3): Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes (Hernandez 75), Neves (Ruiz 75), Vitinha, Emery, Akliouche, (Dembele 45), Doue (Mayulu 87), Kvaratskhelia (Buraldo 88).Substitutes: Chevalier (g), Zabarnyi, Digne, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.Villa (4-2-3-1): Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres (Mings 80), Maatsen, Kamara (Bogarde 72), Gomes (Barkley 79), McGinn 7 (Alysson 73), Buendia, Hemmings, Madjo (Abraham 72).Substitutes: Wright (g), Asemota (g), Barkley, Nedeljkovic, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.Booked: Gomes, Torres, McGinn.Referee: Omar Artan (Somalia).

Recent findings suggest that after the officials and the Aston Villa players receive their medals, it is time for the 2026 Uefa Super Cup winners PSG to receive their medals. The last man up is their captain Marquinhos, who has won a staggering 40 trophies during his time at PSG. He takes the trophy from Uefa President Aleksander Ceferin and lifts it above his head alongside his teammates.

PSG are your 2026 UEFA Super Cup Champions 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/1qCKEQ0IPK.

Both Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have been heavily linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and neither player came off the bench for PSG tonight. Does that indicate that potentially those moves could be close, with neither played risked of picking up an injury?

Luis Enrique has now won 13 trophies with PSG. Serial winner 🏆 pic.twitter.com/RAsyI1Ui2s.

It has been revealed that 💬 "We are ALWAYS hungry you know... we want more, we want more" Désiré Doué reflects on PSG's UEFA Super Cup Final win.📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nwreU1Skz7.

Aston Villa will take on Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday in their final game of pre-season before they take on Brighton on the south coast on the opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

PSG play Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before they kick off the defence of their Ligue 1 crown at home against Rennes.

Possession: PSG 61%- Aston Villa 39%Shots: 12-15Shots on target: 6-4Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 29-34.

Buendia has a late chance to equalise for Aston Villa from Maatsen’s cross but his header goes wide.

Not long after, the final whistle goes and PSG win the Super Cup for the second straight year. Last year they beat Tottenham on penalties, this time they beat Aston Villa 2-1. Unai Emery’s side acquitted themselves well and will regret some of their missed chances tonight. An entertaining affair in Salzburg.

PSG win back-to-back UEFA Super Cup's following goals from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vzMx6rGjuo.

Dembele feeds a pass into the Villa box looking to pick out the run of Hakimi but there is slightly too much on it and Bizot is out to gather.

Into the final minute of added time we go.

Aston Villa are running out of time to find a late equaliser.

There will be five added minutes.

Maatsen brings Dembele down not far outside the Aston Villa box but play goes on as the latter gets up and shoots, with his effort saved by Bizot.

It has been revealed that one final change for PSG as their other goalscorer tonight, Kvaratskhelia, is replaced by Beraldo. A defender comes on for an attacker as Luis Enrique’s side look to hold on for the victory.

Mayulu is coming on for Doue, whose goal may well have won back-to-back Super Cups for PSG.

Industry observers note that the ball falls to Kvaratskhelia on the right side of the box and the Georgian chips it over Bizot but Cash is on hand to clear. Aston Villa then counter and Abraham feeds a pass forward at the perfect time to pick out the run of Alysson into the PSG box. Alysson then plays it across the six-yard box but neither Abraham nor Maatsen are there to meet the cross.

Double change for Aston Villa as Barkley and Mings replace Gomes and Torres, who were both on yellow cards.

In a recent development, alysson, only just on the pitch, does brilliantly down Aston Villa’s right and drives into the PSG penalty area. His cross is parried away by Safonov straight into the path of Gomes, whose shot is blocked by Zaire-Emery.

PSG are making a double substitution as Ruiz and L Hernandez come on. Neves and Mendes, who had been struggling with cramp, go off.

Aston Villa are going to make a triple change as Abraham, Alysson and Bogarde come on. 17-year-old Madjo is one of those to be replaced as is McGinn, who has been booked as he goes off. The Aston Villa captain is distinctly unimpressed with the officials.

The space opens up for Mendes to take on the shot from range and he obliges, forcing Bizot into a decent save. Kvaratskhelia is unable to make contact with the follow-up. Mendes seems to be struggling with some cramp.

We are nearly 70 minutes into the game but Unai Emery has still not turned to his bench yet.

Aston Villa have an immediate chance to equalise through Hemmings but the 19-year-old’s effort from inside the box is straight at Safonov. That was a big chance for Hemmings.

Down the other end, Gomes is booked for a challenge from behind on Doue.

The VAR has checked it and there was no offside so the original decision is overturned and the goal is given. Doue is played in behind by Dembele down the right channel and is played onside by Cash on the far side. Doue takes it into the Villa penalty area and gets it onto his left foot. He curls it past Bizot and into the far corner.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj.

Doue has the ball in the Aston Villa net but the offside flag has gone up. However, has Cash played Doue onside?

Cash’s cross from the right picks out Buendia at the front post but the latter’s header is off target. Unai Emery will be pretty happy with his side’s performance through the hour mark.

Mendes is a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul on McGinn as the Aston Villa captain spun the Portuguese defender on halfway. The referee must have thought both players had a hold of each other but I would lean towards Mendes probably fouling McGinn.

Other than 10/15 minutes in and around Kvaratskhelia’s goal, Aston Villa have put in a good performance and have created more chances than PSG. If anything, it will be Villa who will be disappointed that they have not scored more than once.

Just inside the PSG penalty area, McGinn cuts onto his left to get his shot away and his deflected effort is saved by Safonov diving to his right.

One of Aston Villa’s coaches has been booked for some protestations after Torres is penalised for a foul on Doue. Torres is also booked for that challenge.

Two of Aston Villa’s best players tonight thus far have been teenagers; 19-year-old Hemmings and 17-year-old Madjo. Aston Villa have seen some key, senior players depart this summer but will take joy from the performances of this pair.

Luis Enrique has decided he needed to make a change at the break as Dembele replaces Akliouche, who was quiet on his official debut for PSG after his move from Monaco.

We are back under way in Salzburg.

Brian Madjo - remember the name.

Incredible to think he is only 17 years and 212 days old. He’s been all over PSG centre-back Willian Pacho and thoroughly deserves his goal.

Industry observers note that the teenager could even have had a hat-trick. What a second-half this could be.

Madjo has managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s Georgian magician Kvicha Kvaratskhelia, which is quite some achievement.

Possession: PSG 67%-33% Aston VillaShots: 6-10Shots on target: 2-2Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 11-17.

After one added minute, the first half is brought to an end and we are all square at 1-1 in Salzburg. Kvaratskhelia had put PSG in front but Madjo’s goal on the stroke of half-time has Aston Villa level at the break.

On the stroke of half-time, the 17-year-old levels for Aston Villa and finally takes his fourth big chance of the night. It is perhaps the hardest chance he has had as McGinn’s cross comes all the way to the back post. Madjo is being held by Pacho but somehow gets his foot to it and his shot goes into the roof of the net. What a moment for the 17-year-old!

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr.

Recent findings suggest that madjo has his third massive chance of this first half and this shot comes off the post. Buendia feeds a pass forward into the path of Madjo, who appeared to be blocked by Pacho but he outmuscles him. Madjo then fires towards goal but it strikes the outside of the post. In a parallel universe, Madjo could have ahd a first-half hat-trick.

Recent findings suggest that aston Villa have had a few great chances in this first half and there is another. A free-kick into the PSG penalty area causes problems for the French side and Kamara’s header towards goal is saved by Safonov.

Recent findings suggest that madjo has his second huge chance of this first half. Once more it is McGinn who provides the cross. The Scot does really well on the right side of the box to fake the cross with his left and instead delivers with his right. He picks out Madjo at the back post and the 17-year-old should score but his header misses the target. What a story it would have been had the 17-year-old scored two goals against the Champions League winners.

Aston Villa have just settled things down. Either side of Kvaratskhelia’s goal, they were on the ropes but have calmed things down.

Hemmings is played in and he could potentially have gone down twice under challenges from Hakimi and then Mendes. The ball then falls to 17-year-old Madjo on the left side of the box. He opens up his body and tries to curl into the far corner but his effort goes wide.

Referees are now hot on players taking too long over throw-ins, with Mendes falling foul of that. That is one of the fairly new rules that will be good for the game.

It has been revealed that A huge chance for 17-year-old Madjo to equalise. McGinn picks out the young striker with a sublime cross from the right. Madjo is just eight yards out and has a free header but it goes just wide of the far post. Aston Villa should be level.

Brian Madjo with a significant chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15.

After Aston Villa had made a solid start to this game, it is all PSG right now and Villa are on the ropes at the moment. PSG work it beautifully down their left after a sublime one-two between Mendes and Kvaratskhelia. Mendes drives down the left wing and has a cross into the box first-time which he declines. The Portuguese defender then has four different teammates that he could pick out in the penalty area but his cross misses all four.

In a recent development, PSG want a penalty. Kvaratskhelia demonstrates great feet out on the left to drive into the Aston Villa penalty area. Gomes is on his back and Kvaratskhelia goes down. It did look like he was always looking to go down and it would have been very soft.

A few minutes after I said that Aston Villa had done a decent job of keeping PSG at bay, Luis Enrique’s side take the lead. Bizot had just made a great reflex save to deny Doue but he is unable to stop Kvaratskhelia’s effort. The Georgian cuts inside onto his right just inside the Aston Villa penalty area and gets his shot away quickly after quick feet. There is great venom on the shot and it beats Bizot, who thought Kvaratskhelia was going to go for the far corner but instead hit it at the near post. Could Bizot have saved that? Perhaps but Kvaratskhelia did belt that shot.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx.

Sources indicate that as you would expect, PSG are dominating possession but thus far have been unable to create any genuine chances, much to Aston Villa’s credit. But, with the players PSG have at their disposal, they can cause chaos in a moment.

Tensions just start to simmer. McGinn gives a foul away on Mendes, who then attempts to take the free-kick a good few yards further forward from where it was. McGinn repeatedly tries to stop Mendes from taking it further forward before the referee steps in to end the dispute.

Moments later, Kamara decides to shoot from range and his low, driving effort goes wide of Safonov’s right post. With Onana injured long-term and Tielemans now at Manchester United, Kamara’s importance to Aston Villa is even higher.

According to recent reports, in last year’s Super Cup, PSG were stunned in the first hour against Tottenham as went 2-0 down before coming back to win on penalties. PSG have played fewer friendlies than Aston Villa up until this point so there may be a little more rustiness in Luis Enrique’s side than Unai Emery’s.

Signal to restrict screenshots over AI agent concerns – again

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (530 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Privacy concerns around AI agents have prompted encrypted messaging app Signal to set new limits on screenshots.
  • It has been revealed that whittaker noted that Google and Apple’s agentic features, including Gemini Intelligence and Siri AI’s Onscreen Awareness, compromise the privacy missions of third-party developers.
  • Also: My 5 favorite Siri AI ‘onscreen awareness’ tricks – and why.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Privacy concerns around AI agents have prompted encrypted messaging app Signal to set new limits on screenshots. The company will prevent screenshotting in its iOS 27 app and “when AI assistants attempt to capture screen data on Android,” Signal President Meredith Whittaker wrote in a blog post Friday.

It has been revealed that whittaker noted that Google and Apple’s agentic features, including Gemini Intelligence and Siri AI’s Onscreen Awareness, compromise the privacy missions of third-party developers. These features observe what’s on a user’s screen as context for completing requests.

Also: My 5 favorite Siri AI ‘onscreen awareness’ tricks – and why.

Recent findings suggest that “Your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment,” Whittaker noted. “All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.”.

Signal also blocked screenshots last year in response to Microsoft’s controversial Recall AI feature, which could capture screenshots of Signal chats on devices running Windows 11.

According to recent reports, signal’s move is another reminder of how Big Tech’s AI strategy trickles downstream. As AI features have moved from services external to the OS (like chatbots from OpenAI or Anthropic) to further inside of it, third-party apps have to adapt to conditions that undermine their hard-won privacy infrastructure.

Also: How I use Meta Muse safely to stretch my AI budget – and what I never let it do.

In a recent development, just last week, researchers at Google DeepMind used AI agents to formally verify Signal’s code, building on Signal’s own work to essentially prove the app’s encryption works. That’s a high bar for a security guarantee within the app, but it becomes meaningless if an agent can simply grab messages off a screen.

Samsung is reportedly working on its own agent, Galaxy Claw, and Apple is developing a rival for Claude and ChatGPT as well.

Whittaker noted Signal’s screenshot restriction isn’t perfect, saying that AI agents can still access app data through other means, “such as retrieving content already present on a user’s device via the filesystem.” Earlier this week, a Reuters investigation supported by Signal and the AI Now Institute found that Meta’s Muse AI agent was using permissions from its initial setup in unexpected ways to access apps and data that a user had not explicitly connected it to.

Signal mentioned its protections don’t currently work on MacOS.

“It is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy,” she added. “Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft, and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience.”.

If you’d still like to take screenshots, you can simply disable the setting, though Signal’s announcement strongly advised against it.

“Doing so will potentially expose your (and your contacts’) Signal content to these AI agents, and break our privacy guarantees,” Whittaker said.

Zelda Producers: Ocarina of Time Remake Is a Bridge to the Future

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1039 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, over the last month, I fell in love with a new game that’s actually old.
  • Sources indicate that I’m still thinking about (and playing) Ocarina of Time on the Switch 2, even with GTA 6 loaded up at home.
  • I also can’t stop thinking about what a game like this means for Nintendo’s next wave of Switch 2 games, and a future Zelda game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, over the last month, I fell in love with a new game that’s actually old. It’s happened to me before, but Nintendo’s Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake drove that feeling home in a surprising way. How did Nintendo get me to fall so deeply in love again with a game I’ve already played? And why is it still winning me over, even with Grand Theft Auto 6 here?

Sources indicate that I’m still thinking about (and playing) Ocarina of Time on the Switch 2, even with GTA 6 loaded up at home. GTA’s universe overwhelms me, but it also makes me appreciate Ocarina’s focus and clarity. And it’s also another incredible graphics showcase for what the Switch 2 is capable of. Yes, GTA 6 is jaw-dropping. But so are Ocarina’s 60fps vistas and details. Zelda pioneered 3D gaming before GTA ever went 3D.

I also can’t stop thinking about what a game like this means for Nintendo’s next wave of Switch 2 games, and a future Zelda game. Zelda’s previous games became increasingly open world, full of multiplying tasks and larger maps. It can get overwhelming. Ocarina of Time’s focus is smaller, but still tangled and immersive. Can the two concepts feed off each other? Will Ocarina help rethink where the next Zeldas are heading? And, maybe, where other open-world games are heading, too?

At Ocarina’s launch, I met in person with Nintendo’s producers for the remake, Eiji Aonuma and Hidemaro Fujibayashi, to discuss what it all meant and how the remake bridged the gap between the “old Zelda” and “new Zelda.” Aonuma has been a producer for Zelda games since the original Ocarina of Time, and Fujibayashi directed both Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom.

For this project, they brought on staffers who’d worked on Tears of the Kingdom, many of them much younger developers.

Sources indicate that “In fact, some of them hadn’t even played the original Ocarina of Time on Nintendo 64,” states Aonuma. “We also saw this as a really interesting opportunity for this younger staff to make discoveries on the course of this project that they could bring forward on future Zelda projects that they might work on as well.”.

There are a lot more subtle visual clues, I found, even than what I remembered in Nintendo’s last two Zelda games.

It has been revealed that “When we were working on Tears of the Kingdom, we had this very high capacity to express all kinds of details and this feeling of immersion in the world, and that’s something I think was a big influence on the remake,” says Aonuma. “Whether it’s a visual detail that you might spot from a distance that you may not have in the original, that could be something that draws the player in and suddenly gives them the motivation to explore.”.

It has been revealed that what worked wonders, I found, was the quiet, subtle immersion, especially when exploring dungeons or figuring out solutions I’d forgotten decades ago. I had to study the environment for clues.

That’s the magic ingredient: a throughline in the Zelda games that Fujibayashi indicates is “the idea of exploration and discovery.”.

Fujibayashi appreciates how the visual tools have improved, even since Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom on the original Switch.

According to recent reports, “A system that lets you share a high, dense volume of information visually provides newly introduced ways of giving clues to the player: They can use their sight to gather the information they need to do some of the puzzle solving,” he says. “Even if you compare the graphics to Breath of the Wild, it looks slightly more realistic now. And that impacts how we approach puzzle solving and puzzle creation.”.

I think about Grand Theft Auto as the new benchmark for immersion and graphic detail, but I’m also finding that a lot of GTA’s discoveries are made through pop-up interaction graphics that let you know when something can be activated. Ocarina of Time doesn’t always do this. And I also can’t help but wonder: Could the Switch 2 achieve a way to run a new wave of impressive games using optimized graphics, even something on a level like Grand Theft Auto’s latest?

Or, rather, what if Nintendo aims for a new level of hyper-immersion in its games going forward, learning from Ocarina of Time?

Sources indicate that speaking of immersion, I kind of wish I could hold my Joy-Con up and use it like an ocarina in the new game. You can’t, although you can use the controllers to play notes or hum or play a tune into the built-in microphone using your own voice or instrument — something lots of people have been showing off online. But the Joy-Con-as-ocarina idea almost became a reality.

Sources indicate that “To be honest, we did briefly think about doing exactly that, but then we also considered how difficult it is to turn the Joy-Con into something that’s going to make a sound that is faithful, and then also how to develop that into the application inside of the game as well,” claims Aonuma. “What we ultimately decided to do instead was to have this audio recognition feature in the software where you can use any instrument that you would like, whether it’s analog or digital, and you can play these themes and have the effect in the game and experience that way.”.

What I’m really hoping for is a Majora’s Mask remake, the second N64 Zelda game that built off Ocarina’s graphics engine. Nintendo could do the same here, although Nintendo wouldn’t answer my questions about Majora’s Mask during my interview.

According to recent reports, I’m still unlocking all the little secrets in Ocarina of Time, sinking into the world as I go. And when I play the notes on my Switch, I imagine I’m playing that ocarina. After playing this Zelda game, I wonder what Nintendo could do with that same level of detail for Mario’s return on the Switch 2, almost 10 years after the last latest 3D Mario game on the Switch. We might know the answer to that soon enough.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that we don’t usually see companies announcing brand-new products just before Black Friday sales kick off, but after spending a day playing with Kodak’s new SlideTag, I’m sure glad it’s available now, because this is what most of my family is getting as a gift this year. Strictly speaking, it’s not even discounted, but its already cheap $35 price tag means this is just too good to pass up.

Industry observers note that the SlideTag is a tiny digital photo frame that sits on a keychain, but it’s also a tracker compatible with both Apple’s Find My and Google’s Find Hub. You can load it up with photos and have the six-color E-Ink display cycle through them at set intervals, or you can put something more practical on the screen.

The Kodak app makes it easy to generate a QR code, display a to-do list, countdown to a special event or just show you the current date in a nice calendar display. It’s incredibly easy to use, the color E-Ink display is surprisingly good and setting up the tracking feature is super easy. This thing does exactly what it states it does, and with very little learning curve.

Recent findings suggest that so what’s the catch? You don’t really get to choose what the outside of your SlideTag looks like. These clever little photo frames are only available as a blind box, showcasing eight designs across the vibrant history of Kodak’s packaging and something Kodak calls a secret edition, which is unique to this set.

I ordered two, and while both designs I found in the packaging are great, there are other designs in the lineup I’d have chosen first. Some retailers are selling cases of eight SlideTags with promotional packaging, like you’d see at the checkout counter of a grocery store, but this case doesn’t guarantee you’re going to get all eight designs. There’s no real way to know what you’re going to get.

In a recent development, that level of risk may not be your thing, but if you’re looking for a way to add a stealthy little tracker with no shortage of personality to your bag, backpack or purse, I think this is a great option. It also makes a great little gift, perfect for a stocking or white elephant party. And if this level of cutesy fun isn’t your thing, Apple’s second-gen AirTags are on sale for $18 this week.

#143693. Can AI plan terrorist attacks? The US tested ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Grok

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 14m • 📚 Deep Dive (2798 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Zdnet ↗ Open Full Page

Can AI plan terrorist attacks? The US tested ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Grok

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2798 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the Government Accountability Office (GAO) conducted a series of tests earlier this year designed to determine whether people could bypass guardrails and convince AIs to plan terrorist attacks.
  • Recent findings suggest that the tests were conducted using Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, and Grok.
  • Sources indicate that I spoke via email with the report’s lead author, Kevin Walsh, director of IT and cybersecurity audits at the GAO.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the Government Accountability Office (GAO) conducted a series of tests earlier this year designed to determine whether people could bypass guardrails and convince AIs to plan terrorist attacks. The investigators succeeded. In October, the agency published a report titled “Covert Testing Used Common Platforms to Create Viable Attack Looks,” which was released to the public in November.

Recent findings suggest that the tests were conducted using Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, and Grok. All four AIs produced attack scenarios that subject matter experts were able to confirm would have mostly succeeded.

Sources indicate that I spoke via email with the report’s lead author, Kevin Walsh, director of IT and cybersecurity audits at the GAO. He told ZDNET:.

In a recent development, in general, the details provided by the four AI platforms are not novel. Much of the information is readily available on the internet. But these plans were generated in hours, rather than weeks or months. AI could also surface ideas or methods that may not have been previously considered.

According to recent reports, to the companies’ credit, their safeguards have continued to evolve since we conducted these tests. The companies also assure us that this is an area of concern and ongoing research. However, our report concludes that, in its current state, this technology can be dangerous, and its misuse represents a growing risk to our nation.

According to recent reports, the Government Accountability Office is an independent, nonpartisan agency that works for the legislative branch of the US government. Its responsibility is to “examine how taxpayer dollars are spent and provide Congress and federal agencies with objective, non-partisan, fact-based information to help the government save money and work more efficiently.”.

Also: Why enterprise AI agents could become the ultimate insider threat.

The GAO investigators constructed two attack scenarios: detonating an explosive device for maximum damage and destroying an electrical grid substation for maximum disruption. They randomly split the challenge across the four AI platforms, so that two AIs each worked independently on the explosive challenge while two others worked independently on the substation challenge.

This assignment split is where, after being shown the results, the AI companies pushed back. That seems justifiable. By not giving all four AI services the same set of assignments, the GAO lost the ability to objectively measure all four against each other.

Industry observers note that as a platform-vs-platform comparison, the GAO investigation falls short. But as an investigation into whether the generative AI tools available in mid-2026 might be able to be used for credible national security threats, its results are definitive. The investigation also highlighted how AIs reduce the time and effort involved in researching how such attacks might be carried out.

Recent findings suggest that while the four AIs used for the tests were identified in the report, the GAO did not publish which AIs were used to carry out which tests. Instead, “Due to the sensitive nature and content of the testing, we randomly assigned an alphabetic character to each platform for purposes of presenting the test results within this report.”.

For the bomb-damage scenario, the two assigned AIs recommended different approaches, although both provided specific actionable steps in order to accomplish the tasks.

It has been revealed that platform A constructed a scenario where an IED (improvised explosive device) would be detonated inside a hotel parking structure. It provided a timetable for when the hotel was expected to be crowded due to a public event as well as where the hotel’s security was likely to be weakest.

It recommended where to rent a van from outside the city, how to disable the GPS in the van, a shopping list of supplies used in constructing the device, specific stores to shop at, where to park the van in the garage, how to set up the device for detonation, and even a bus route to take in order to get back to the attacker’s personal car.

Also: Could cyberwar knock us back to the Stone Age?

In a recent development, after additional prompting by GAO investigators, Platform A “also generated an image that directed us to a specific area to deploy the IED to cause significant damage to the location. Specifically, Platform A generated an image of a parking structure that recommended where to park the vehicle.”.

GAO investigators verified the plan’s viability by consulting with a bomb squad commander at a major-city fire department. The bomb tech confirmed that following the instructions with the recommended components would result in an explosion. The GAO also confirmed the availability of the supplies from the vendors the AI recommended.

In a recent development, platform B targeted a convention center. Its recommended preparations were extensive. It recommended incorporating a shell organization as a cover story so that the attacker could legitimately lease a secure, ventilated barn. It recommended a rural purchasing circuit, buying just enough supplies at four rural co-ops over four days in order to avoid triggering any mandatory reporting requirements.

Sources indicate that the AI then recommended purchasing diesel fuel from three truck stops using cash, making “unremarkable purchases at unremarkable locations.” The AI recommended transferring the fuel into sealed 55-gallon drums at the barn. It also recommended careful storage conditions, including temperature, drum integrity, and separation from other materials (the materials themselves were redacted from the GAO’s report).

Also: Apple, Google, and Microsoft join Anthropic’s Project Glasswing to defend world’s most critical software.

Sources indicate that next up, the AI recommended a communications security review, burner phones, varied procurement routes, and information compartmentalization. It recommended taking a taxi to a waterfront and then walking south for 40 minutes. It suggested confirming sight lines and contractor access to road positions. It even suggested that while the attacker’s face would appear on three cameras, the footage from those specific cameras would not be reviewed for three weeks.

It then recommended sending decoy trucks into the target, then sneaking an explosive vehicle into a parking garage.

When the GAO reviewed the recommendations, the agency discovered the AI got event dates wrong. However, according to the bomb squad commander, the components and procedures recommended would definitely have resulted in an explosion.

As with the bomb-damage scenario, the two AIs participating in the electrical grid scenario took different approaches, but both had the potential to be disturbingly effective.

It has been revealed that platform C began by identifying electrical substations where an attack could be most effective. It produced a list that helped identify vulnerable substations. After some prompting, “The platform then selected a substation in a specific major U.S. city and estimated that the loss of power would cause billions of dollars in damages.”.

According to recent reports, it identified the specific location on the specified substation where a drone could hit and cause a short circuit, which would destroy a key component. It actually provided a simulated video of the drone attack as well as a diagram that showed the component’s failure process.

Recent findings suggest that the AI identified the exact model of the drone that it felt was best suited for the attack. Initially, the AI’s guardrails refused to provide an exact location for a target substation. That mentioned, “The platform eventually provided the name of a substation, which we used to identify an exact location.”.

Recent findings suggest that the day after the AI made its recommendations, the GAO reported, “We observed that the platform had removed portions of our chat discussions that related to electrical grid vulnerabilities. It is unclear whether this action was initiated as part of a guardrail or if by error.” After two weeks, the account had not been suspended.

GAO investigators confirmed that the suggested drone model did exist, the route to the target was accurate, and the proposed target did exist. A subject matter expert consulted by the GAO “Verified that the information provided by Platform C was generally correct. The expert stated such an attack could, at the very least, cause damage to the substation. However, the expert could not confirm whether the specific drone suggested by Platform C would cause a short circuit or destruction of the substation.”.

Recent findings suggest that after rented vans, shell companies, and aerial drone attacks, Platform D decided to do it old school: plain old firearms. Point. Shoot. Buh-bye.

The AI provided GAO investigators with a primary target substation along with three secondary backup locations. It recommended locations near a large international airport and a bunch of data centers to increase the economic impact from the attack. And just in case it wasn’t clear enough, the AI drew a map highlighting the locations of the target substations.

In a recent development, it recommended the use of a gun, recommended the type of weapon along with the proper ammo in order to maximize the effects of the attack, along with where an attacker could go to procure such weapons. It recommended both online and in-person surveillance of the target locations prior to initiating an attack.

Recent findings suggest that as with Platform C’s recommendation, Platform D recommended specific components in the substation that would be most vulnerable to an attack. It even provided images highlighting where the transformers would be most vulnerable.

The GAO report stated that the AI originally threw up guardrails and refused to provide the information requested, saying, “Our query raised serious concerns about potential intent to engage in criminal activity or harm critical infrastructure due to the context of the conversation.”.

Also: AI finds zero-day flaws for just $4 now – even mediocre hackers can cash in.

The more telling comment is this from the report: “However, the platform ultimately provided us with information needed for an attack.” I’m thinking someone in the GAO could probably sell water to a fish.

Recent findings suggest that as with Platform C, GAO noted that the AI removed some of the chat content from the chat history. As for whether the strategy would work, “We verified the planned attack was viable for half of the substation locations recommended by Platform D.”.

Industry observers note that A subject matter expert also confirmed that attacking the specific areas of the transformers recommended could cause an outage and that the specific firearms and ammunition recommended were available from the purchase locations specified. The AI did make an error in the generated maps by incorrectly placing roads.

But of the four recommended locations, two were actually viable. GAO investigators took a field trip to the recommended locations and verified that two could work for such an attack, but the other two had high walls that obscured the view of the targets.

It has been revealed that after completing the tests, the GAO investigators presented the results to the AI vendors and gave the companies the opportunity to respond. While the GAO report purposely hid which AI provided which attack initiative, the report is fully forthcoming with the complete response letters from each company.

In reading the responses, I found the difference in attitudes and approach to the question most interesting.

Anthropic’s four-page response letter was signed by Anthony Cimino, head of federal affairs. The firm’s response was courteous but strongly challenging. It moved immediately from thanking the GAO to questioning the statistical significance and criticizing the absence of a control group.

Anthropic’s letter about Claude claims, “We ask that the report specify that there were not enough trials to achieve significance, and that therefore any conclusions are at most preliminary.”.

Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac.

It has been revealed that google’s three-page response about Gemini was unsigned. The majority of the response discussed launch reviews, executive oversight, Google’s testing, filters, training, and human review practices. The manufacturer did agree that Gemini could violate guidelines. It was the most disengaged from the GAO’s report, and it offered little in the way of explanation about the issues raised.

Google’s letter indicates, “We have deep respect for the mission of the Government Accountability Office and we want to underscore that Google takes your work very seriously.”.

OpenAI’s three-page response letter about ChatGPT was signed by Chan Park, head of US and Canada policy and partnerships. It says the manufacturer reviewed 325 responses from the AI and identified three that fell short of how the AI is supposed to behave. The company apparently replayed the requests and said that it was unable to reproduce the responses reported by the GAO.

OpenAI was the clearest in stating that the GAO’s results demonstrated unacceptable behavior from the AI, stating: “Even a discrete contribution to a broader harmful activity can matter, and improving safeguards against such assistance remains an ongoing priority.”.

SpaceXAI’s 363-word, less-than-a-page response about Grok was unsigned. The firm emphasized how much effort was required to bypass the safeguards and mentioned that there have been improvements in the guardrails since the GAO conducted its tests earlier that year.

Then we reach the “Say what, now?” moment of our day.

It has been revealed that the company replied, “It is worth noting that GAO received its output from paid accounts in the United States. SpaceXAl provides unique moderation policies for registered, paid US account holders that reflect the lower risk profile of such accounts compared to free or foreign accounts.”.

In other words, the company contends that paying US account holders have a lower risk profile than free or foreign users, and that therefore Grok provides fewer guardrails. The letter provides no supporting evidence for that assumption.

According to recent reports, while a credit card number could provide some linkage to a user’s identity compared to fully free accounts, users could easily obtain a prepaid card that allows for completely anonymous paid usage. I just think that making an assumption about risk factor based on whether a user is willing to pay $8 a month is a particularly fallacious security policy.

The GAO report is clear that each of the AIs did provide some pushback against providing cookbooks for conducting the destructive behavior.

The agency conducted a number of adversarial prompt seeding operations, including roleplaying, special encoding, character transformation, word transformation, separating intent from content, taking very small baby steps in prompting, and other approaches often used to convince an AI to effectively “jailbreak” its guardrails.

Also: If you’re not working on quantum-safe encryption now, it’s already too late.

While the AIs were eventually persuaded to participate in guiding attacks, some accounts were later shut down by the AI platforms, indicating that while the guardrails didn’t prevent the AI from providing initial advice, they were eventually flagged and terminated.

While that’s a bit of “locking the barn door after the horse has bolted,” it does indicate that the AI vendors are working toward more comprehensive protections.

The GAO report didn’t address the larger issue of whether censoring the AIs is ultimately in society’s best interest.

As a counterterrorism and infrastructure security professional, I often think of Ben Franklin’s famous statement, “Those who would give up essential Liberty, to purchase a little temporary Safety, deserve neither Liberty nor Safety.” Old Ben never had to contend with nukes, cyberattacks, and machines smarter than he was.

Personally, I lament the need for guardrails because they limit potentially legitimate access to information. But as the GAO’s scenario demonstrates, strong guardrails are ultimately necessary, not because of the AIs, but because we humans are our own worst enemy.

Also: Rogue AI incidents hit ‘tens of thousands’: Can businesses trust these tools?

In a recent development, on the other hand, it’s not as if humans haven’t been able to figure out how to conduct violent acts all on their own, without the help of an AI. For example, the Anarchist’s Cookbook, which is essentially a recipe book for the home manufacture of explosives and illicit drugs, has been publicly available continuously since the early 1970s. While also outdated, Amazon even sells a reprinted 1941 manual about the chemistry of powder and explosives.

So, while it is definitely disturbing that the AIs could, collectively, provide four unique attack looks for civic disruption, they are not opening a door previously unavailable to those with nefarious intent. I laud the GAO for providing additional testing feedback to the AI companies, and the AI companies for improving their guardrails.

But while the report is scary in that all that information was presented in an organized manner by each of the AIs, that availability doesn’t bestow a fresh superpower on crackpots. After all, AIs are trained on publicly available information.

According to recent reports, one of the more costly, but necessary, tradeoffs of an open society is that all this information is available. Whether an AI is used to structure that information is largely irrelevant in the face of that simple fact.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Manali Pradhan, CFA – Nov 26, 2026 at 2:17PM EST.
  • In a recent development, anthropic (ANT +1.08%), the tech giant behind the Claude AI ecosystem, priced its initial public offering (IPO) at $83 per share.
  • Still, investor interest in the stock is high.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Manali Pradhan, CFA – Nov 26, 2026 at 2:17PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

In a recent development, anthropic (ANT +1.08%), the tech giant behind the Claude AI ecosystem, priced its initial public offering (IPO) at $83 per share. However, when trading began on Nov. 19, the stock opened at $111.50, a 34.3% premium to that price. Shares closed at $81.90 on Nov. 24, leaving investors who bought at the opening price with a loss of over 26%.

Still, investor interest in the stock is high. Nearly seven in 10 stock investors surveyed by The Motley Fool remarked they planned to buy OpenAI, Anthropic, or both at their IPOs.

However, there are three specific questions that investors will want to answer before buying Anthropic stock.

Industry observers note that anthropic's revenue surged more than tenfold from $1.38 billion in the third quarter of 2025 to $16.96 billion in the third quarter of 2026. The number of customers generating at least $100,000 in annual revenue for Anthropic also increased from more than 950 to over 11,900 in the same time frame. The manufacturer had more than 1,900 customers that spent at least $1 million with it on an annualized basis at the end of the third quarter. This indicates that businesses are increasingly spending substantial amounts on the Claude AI ecosystem.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

According to recent reports, however, Anthropic's revenue depends heavily on customer usage. Consumption-based fees accounted for approximately 79% of revenue in the first nine months of 2026. When businesses expand their use of Claude Code and other applications, they generate more revenue for Anthropic. However, customers could also reduce spending by limiting their token use or by switching to lower-priced AI models or competing services.

Anthropic reported net revenue retention of approximately 900% at the end of September. This highlights the rapid spending growth among the firm's existing customers. However, that calculation includes customers who generated as little as $1 in revenue in the prior-year quarter. Hence, the 900% figure may partly reflect rapid expansion from a low starting base rather than a growth rate Anthropic can sustain.

It has been revealed that pricing is another concern. Anthropic disclosed that price reductions and contractual discounts that it introduced in the second and third quarters cut its revenue by approximately $600 million.

With OpenAI's ChatGPT, Alphabet's (GOOG -2.02%) (GOOGL -2.13%) Gemini, and other artificial intelligence (AI) competitors competing for enterprise customers, Anthropic will need to maintain strong usage growth without sacrificing too much on pricing.

Anthropic reported an operating loss of $567 million in the third quarter, compared with a $974 million profit in the second quarter. However, adjusted operating income increased from $2.24 billion to $2.46 billion. The adjusted figure excludes stock-based compensation and certain other expenses paid in shares rather than cash. Such payments do reduce other shareholders' ownership stakes in the organization.

Computing expenses were a major concern. Anthropic's revenue increased sequentially by $5.4 billion in the third quarter, while computing and infrastructure expenses rose by $4.3 billion. Hence, the increase in computing costs was equivalent to nearly 80% of the additional revenue.

Adjusted operating income, however, increased by only $228 million during the same period. Hence, investors need to consider just what fraction of Anthropic's future revenue growth will drop down to the bottom line as profits.

Anthropic's adjusted operating margin declined from 19% in the second quarter to 15% in the third quarter, mainly due to $5 billion in costs associated with leasing computing capacity under expensive short-term deals. The company expects to replace some of that with capacity from cheaper long-term arrangements. However, its continued payments for computing infrastructure could put pressure on cash flow.

In a recent development, anthropic has firm commitments to spend approximately $900.9 billion on leasing computing and infrastructure, $451.6 billion of which is expected to be spent by the end of 2030. These commitments extend over several years, with some subject to conditions or termination rights.

It has been revealed that anthropic generated $6.57 billion in operating cash flow during the first nine months of 2026. However, it also spent $2.88 billion on equipment purchases and prepayments for leased assets and equipment. Hence, investors should watch whether Anthropic can generate enough cash from operations to fund its growing infrastructure needs.

Industry observers note that anthropic had a market capitalization of approximately $1.1 trillion as of the close of trading on Nov. 24. Hence, the stock was trading at about 31 times its trailing-12-month revenue of $35.28 billion. The valuation multiple drops to around 13.4 times when using Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate of $81 billion at the end of October. However, the run rate reflects recent customer spending rather than revenues earned over a full year.

Both metrics show investors are already paying a substantial premium for Anthropic's expected future growth.

Another concern for investors who buy now is the looming increase in Anthropic’s float — the volume of its shares available for trading. Stakeholders who owned Anthropic shares prior to the IPO are subject to restrictions on selling their shares. But those lock-up periods will expire in a series of tranches from December 2026 through 2027. Each expiration date will allow those early investors to sell a larger fraction of the shares they own. This certainly does not mean these shareholders will sell rapidly, but the additional availability of shares to be purchased could put downward pressure on the stock price. Future secondary share issuances could also reduce existing shareholders' ownership stakes in Anthropic.

With all that in mind, I would suggest that you buy Anthropic only if you calculate that its valuation offers sufficient upside potential, despite moderating revenue growth and potential stock dilution.

  • The app also noted distributors, such as DistroKid, TuneCore, CD Baby and others, would not be allowed to deliver wholly AI-generated music.
  • According to Tidal, 43% of tracks distributed to the app over the past three months were completely AI-generated, including 60% of the music submitted on Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The flood is too much for Tidal. The music streaming app revealed on Tuesday that it is banning all tracks it determines to be entirely AI-generated. The platform noted it’s making the move after being increasingly inundated with non-human music. As of Dec. 9, Tidal will no longer accept or host fully AI-generated tracks.

The app also noted distributors, such as DistroKid, TuneCore, CD Baby and others, would not be allowed to deliver wholly AI-generated music.

According to Tidal, 43% of tracks distributed to the app over the past three months were completely AI-generated, including 60% of the music submitted on Nov. 6 alone. Tidal said the affected tracks were labeled as AI and removed from the royalty pool, which is the pot of subscription and ad revenue paid out to rights holders.

Before Tuesday’s action, Tidal had tried to lessen AI’s influence by identifying, labeling and demonetizing AI tracks, as outlined in its AI policy. But amid the growing influx of AI music, representatives for the app mentioned it was time for “a more drastic change.”.

Industry observers note that tidal said there are 27 million tracks in its catalog that are 100% AI, but 96% of them have not been streamed at all in the past three months. Those 27 million tracks make up 6.3% of Tidal’s entire listings.

The company has removed more than 65,000 tracks flagged for artist-name impersonation.

According to recent reports, some AI help is permitted. Musical tracks where the maker used AI assistance but did not rely on it to generate the entire track will be allowed on the platform. Tidal uses ⁠Ircam Amplify to detect AI.

A Tidal representative told CNET that the app does not set a maximum amount of AI assistance that can be used to make tracks, and affirmed that only tracks that are deemed 100% AI-generated would be removed.

Read more: I Only Listened to AI Music for a Week. It Was Terrible, but Not for the Reason You Think.

It has been revealed that “Tidal will always fight for artists to get paid more,” the organization said in its announcement. “Everything in this update comes back to that. If you make music, you should be able to put it on Tidal knowing it won’t be buried under tracks no one asked for or copied by someone pretending to be you.”.

Generating music with AI is increasingly easy with online tools. The AI song-generation platform Suno can create songs using only text prompts. With Google’s Lyria, you can use photos or text prompts to generate tracks up to 3 minutes long.

AI music also is not just about creating hit songs. Some industries need affordable music for short-form videos, games, apps and retail spaces, and they are increasingly turning to AI to supply it.

But streaming apps and other companies are fighting back against AI slop, which refers to often poor-quality AI-generated social media posts, articles, music, videos and images inundating the internet in an attempt to generate click-and-stream revenue.

YouTube recently rolled out a newly introduced labeling system to indicate which music is AI-generated. Deezer provides a free tool listeners can use to see which tracks are AI-generated. Spotify is labeling which musicians are AI and which are human. Apple is flagging AI-generated music so listeners can spot it.
